REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Selection of Individual Consultant)

PEOPLE’S REPUBLIC OF CHINA

World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project)

Loan No.: 9084-CN

Procurement No.: 0733-26093706

Assignment Title: Individual Consulting Services (Project Assistant) – Re-advertisement

Contract No.: HN-IC-7A

The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank to finance the World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of the loan to this consulting service.

The main scope of the consulting services (hereinafter referred to as the “Services”) includes:

1Assist with the day-to-day affairs of the Project Management Office (PMO) and coordinate internal and external communications;

2The Project Assistant shall be responsible for preparing relevant documents to be submitted by the Hainan Provincial Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs to the Provincial PMO and the Project Management Company;

3Provide support for project activities, including preparatory work and on-site support;

4Be responsible for coordination and communication among all parties involved in the Project, including but not limited to the World Bank, sub-project offices, procurement agents, Project Implementing Agencies, project management units, and other relevant entities, ensuring a 100% rate of information synchronization;

5Be responsible for classifying and organizing project-related documents and promptly updating the latest versions of all relevant documents (including hard copies and electronic copies), ensuring real-time version updates and an error rate of no more than 1%;

6Assist in the preparation and logistical support of various project-related activities, such as meetings, training sessions, and field visits;

7Complete other routine tasks assigned by the PMO in a timely manner.

One (1) individual consultant will be selected to serve as the Project Assistant under this consulting service. The estimated total input is 16 person-months, and the expected implementation period of the consulting service is 16 months, from the date of contract signing until the closing date of the World Bank-financed Project, December 31, 2027. The expected commencement date of the consulting service is September 2026.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this consulting service are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

The Hainan Provincial Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (hereinafter referred to as the “Client”) now invites qualified individual consultants to express their interest in providing the consulting service. Interested individual consultants should provide relevant documents (Letter of Bid, Quotation Form, Curriculum Vitae (CV) of the Individual Consultant (in the format specified in “3. Curriculum Vitae (CV) Template for Individual Consultant”), and supporting documents demonstrating that the Individual Consultant meets the “VI. Qualification Requirements” of the TOR, including but not limited to copies of both sides of the identity card, copies of graduation certificate and degree certificate or equivalent educational qualification certificates, supporting documents for relevant work experience, and Letter of Commitment from the Individual Consultant), demonstrating that they possess the qualifications and relevant experience required to perform the service. The specific selection criteria for the individual consultant are as follows:

The Project Assistant should have an appropriate level of professional competence, experience in project management, proficiency in the use of office software, and good writing skills. The specific requirements are as follows:

(I) Basic Requirements

  1. Be a citizen of the People’s Republic of China and be able to work in Haikou City on a full-time basis;
  2. Comply with the laws and regulations of the People’s Republic of China and have no record of violation of laws or disciplines;
  3. Have good conduct and professional ethics;
  4. Possess the physical condition and psychological qualities necessary to perform the duties of the position normally;
  5. Be 40 years old or younger (born on or after January 1, 1986);
  6. Hold a bachelor’s degree or above in Animal Science, Veterinary Medicine, Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Medicine, Economics and Management, or a related field.

(II) Applicants Must Not Fall Under Any of the Following Circumstances (The Individual Consultant shall provide a Letter of Commitment in the format specified in “4. Letter of Commitment from the Individual Consultant”)

  1. Having been subject to any type of criminal punishment;
  2. Having been dismissed from public office;
  3. Being under investigation for violations of laws or disciplines;
  4. Having not yet been released from disciplinary sanctions under Party or government rules;
  5. Being a person subject to conscription who refuses or evades compulsory military service and refuses to make corrections; or being a military service member who, for the purpose of evading military service, refuses to perform duties or deserts the military and has been dismissed from the military, discharged from military service, or held criminally liable in accordance with the law;
  6. Being a person subject to enforcement for dishonesty.

Interested individual consultants should take note of the provisions set forth in Sections 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (the “Procurement Regulations”) (November 2020), which set out the World Bank’s policy on conflicts of interest.

The individual consultant will be selected using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method specified in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested eligible individual consultants may obtain further information from China CNTIC Tendering Co., Ltd. (Contacts: Liu Shuang and Guo Xinyue; Email: liushuang@ck.citic.com, guoxinyue@ck.citic.com), and may inspect and obtain the Request for Expressions of Interest during office hours (i.e., 9:00–17:00, excluding statutory holidays) at the address below.

The Expressions of Interest must be submitted in writing (by hand or by mail) to the address below before 17:00 on September 22, 2026 (the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest).

Sealing and Number of Copies of the Expressions of Interest:

One (1) original hard copy of the Chinese Expressions of Interest and four (4) hard copies of the Chinese Expressions of Interest shall be submitted. The original and copies of the Expressions of Interest shall be separately bound and sealed in the same envelope. The inner and outer envelopes shall bear the following additional identification:

(1) Project Name: World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project);

(2) Contract No. and Title: HN-IC-7A: Individual Consulting Services (Project Assistant) – Re-advertisement.

The Consultant shall also submit, together with the Expressions of Interest, one (1) complete color scanned copy of the original Expressions of Interest in PDF format and one (1) editable electronic copy in Word format, stored on a USB flash drive and separately sealed. In case of any discrepancy between the electronic version and the hard copy, the Chinese original hard copy of the Expressions of Interest shall prevail.

Note: The Consultant shall ensure that the markings on the outer packaging of the submission are consistent with the contents of the Expressions of Interest.

Alternatively, the Consultant shall send the color scanned copy of the original Expressions of Interest in PDF format and one (1) editable electronic copy in Word format to the Procurement Agent’s email address at liushuang@ck.citic.com before the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

 Name of Project: Regional Climate Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa 2 Project (RCRP2).

Project ID: P181308

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Development and Implementation of a Training Program in support of strengthening the capacities of key senior Hydromet and DRR practitioners among the RCRP countries, AU, SADC, ICPAC and other key regional entities.

Reference No. ET-AUC-567618-CS-QCBS

 

 

The African Union Commission has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of The Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda (BIASHARA) 2063 Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Consultancy Services for the Development and Implementation of a Training Program in support of strengthening the capacities of key senior Hydromet and DRR practitioners among the RCRP countries, AU, SADC, ICPAC and other key regional entities 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

 The African Union Commission now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. Firm’s core business: The firm should have a core business on training in hydrology, meteorology, climate sciences, physics, information and knowledge management, disaster risk management , Knowledge of MHEWS / AMHEWAS and has a license from a national or regional professional Body.
  2. Years in Business: The firm should have Minimum of 5 years’ experience in carrying out such trainings.
  3. Specific Experience: The firm should complete a minimum of 5 relevant similar projects financed by the World Bank or International financing Institution.
  4. The firm Should have adoption and use of proven training Quality Assurance measures.
  5. The firm should have demonstrated experience of having undertaken similar assignments in Africa at continental or regional levels
  6. The Firm should have an adequate staff with the required skill and qualification Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultants’ Quality and Cost-based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by October 8, 2026.

 African Union Commission,

Head of Supply Chain Management Division

Building C, 3rd Floor,

P.O Box 3243, Roosevelt Street

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Tel: +251 (0) 11 551 7700 – Ext 4305

Fax: +251 (0) 11 551 0442; +251 11-551-0430

E-mail: Tender@africanunion.org

Terms of Reference

 

Consultancy Services for Development and Implementation of a Training Program in support of strengthening the capacities of key senior Hydromet and DRR practitioners among the RCRP countries, AU, SADC, ICPAC and other key regional entities.

 

  1. Introduction

Africa is facing accelerated social-economic challenges, compounded by hydrometeorological induced disasters such as droughts, floods, tropical cyclones, mudslides and windstorms which have intensified in frequency and magnitude. This upsurge can be attributed, in part, to lack of mainstreaming of disaster risk reduction in development planning, inadequate investment in hydromet and early warning infrastructure, and lack of data management, open access and innovation in systems along with weak financial and human capacity to prepare, anticipate and respond to disaster emergencies. During the last 40 years, Africa has experienced more than 1000 disasters affecting more than 460 million people.  In response to increasing disasters, the African Union Commission (AUC) with the support of the World Bank is implementing the Regional Climate Resilience Programme for Eastern and Southern Africa (RCRP-2) Series of Projects (SOP). This programme is a second operation in the SOPs funded by the World Bank. The programme aims to enhance climate resilience across Eastern and Southern Africa, including the African Union (AU), Comoros, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique and South Sudan.

 

The AUC is an implementing partner, tasked with strengthening regional coordination and capacity building within RCRP-2 countries. The AUC, therefore, seeks to recruit a team of consultants to undertake this assignment within sub-component 1.4: Strengthening capacity on hydromet services, Disaster Risk Management (DRM), and climate finance mobilisation. This sub-component aims to establishing and strengthening standardized regional systems and fostering technical expertise required to effectively respond to climate shocks and build long-term resilience. The training will build and enhance the capacities of RCRP-2 countries to implement the Africa Multi-Hazard Early Warning and Early Action System (AMHEWAS) Programme and enhance capacity of hydromet services to produce actionable forecast, alerts, warning advisories in coordination with AMHEWAS Situation Rooms, National Hydromet Agencies and National Disaster Management Agencies. Consequently, the AUC, in collaboration with the World Bank, seeks to recruit a team of consultants to organise a series of three short training courses (over a period of 6 months) to build the capacity of RCRP-2 countries. The training will cover the capacity needs of hydrometeorological and disaster risk management experts in RCRP-2 countries and respective Regional Economic Communities (RECs), particularly the Southern Africa Community Development (SADC) and IGAD Climate Prediction and Application Centre (ICPAC) as well as the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres and other relevant entities within Africa East and South.

 

  1. Objective of the training programme

The overall objective of the training programme is to strengthen the capacities of representatives from National Hydromet agencies, National DRM agencies, the African Union, Regional Climate Centres, Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres, and DRR situation rooms from SADC and ICPAC regions for improved understanding, analytics, management and access of weather, water and climate information to support decision support tools that aid policy makers.

 

  1. Scope of assignment

The proposed training programme aligns with Component 1.4 of the RCRP-2 project and is a critical mechanism for achieving the Project Development Objective: “To improve resilience to climate- related shocks in Malawi and the Eastern and Southern Africa region, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or emergency, to respond promptly and effectively to it.”

 

  • Synergies between the training programme and the overall RCRP-2 project objectives;

The capacity building initiatives under the AU Commission’s component 1.4 directly contribute to the Project Development Objective (PDO) and Series of Projects objective by addressing critical regional capacity gaps. This training consultancy will be aligned with another activity – Consultancy to support regional hydromet diagnostic, regional engagement, support for systems and capacity building. This training consultancy is to be implemented within the framework of:

 

  • Integrated EWS and DRR preparedness;

The short training programme strengthens the capacity of national and regional institutions including hydromet, DRM agencies and related regional agencies, to strengthen EWS. The programme brings together selected data producers (hydromet) and users (DRM), specifically decision makers to facilitate common operational understanding and procedures. This addresses current data-to-action gaps and ensures that warnings are met with synchronized early actions, directly supporting the objective of responding “promptly and effectively” to shocks. It underpins the successful roll-out of the AMHEWAS programme.

 

  • Need for a Community of Practice for Collaboration and partnerships:

Products produced by National Hydrometeorological Agencies are used by National Disaster Management Agencies and other sectors. Lack of national coordination, collaboration and partnerships results in ineffective use of the information and inadequate preparedness and/or response by weather-dependent sectors. This leads to delayed response time to take anticipatory action by the users of hydrometeorological information. By bringing the relevant institutions in the same training, the training courses will foster interoperability, collaboration and improving the producer-user needs. Fostering a shared community of practice would allow for greater understanding and coordination.

 

  • Regional coordination:

The programme formally strengthens regional mechanisms for cooperation, which are essential for managing transboundary climate and weather-related challenges and harmonizing data and response protocols across borders, a core tenet of the RCRP SOP.

 

The Consultancy will deliver a training program and support the establishment of the abovementioned community of practice. This will contribute to strengthening capacities of country representatives as well as those of AU, Regional Climate Centres, Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres, SADC, and ICPAC. This group will include service producers and end-users across multiple-sectors and within the project participating countries to improve resilience to climate shocks.

 

  1. Tasks of the consultants
  1. Task 1: Develop a defined training strategy including establishing the community of practitioners: The consultants, with support from AU (COP) will establish the COP with due attention to roles, functionalities mandates, qualifications and potential for impact. The consultant team will detail in its inception report the technical approach, methodology, and implementation strategy for the training programme. Based on initial consultations, the consultant firm will confirm the training scope, thematic areas and modalities for training including virtual and in-person trainings.

 

  1. Task 2: Develop training materials: The consultant firm will design detailed training modules for the prioritized thematic areas, with the content covering areas relevant to the design and implementation of multi-hazard early warning systems in RCRP-2 countries, including hazard monitoring and observation systems, Disaster Risk Reduction, data access, management, and use in decision support. The training materials will incorporate practical demonstrations of Multi-hazard early warning systems and align with tools and systems used by the COP. The consultant firm will also include the AMHEWAS system in their training and will be provided with the requisite access. 

 

  1. Task 3: Implement the training program through webinars and at least one advanced training course (in-person) for the COP: The consultant One webinar and one advanced training workshop for the RCRP-2 participating countries (Malawi, Comoros, Madagascar, Mozambique and South Sudan). The AU, ICPAC and SADC SHOC as well as other regional bodies, will also participate in advanced training to strengthen synergies and seamless operations with the RCRP-2 countries. This training workshop will facilitate intensive, localized, and context-specific training and form the basis for strengthening regional transboundary coordination mechanisms. Countries like Malawi and Mozambique, will be given opportunities to share their experiences and practices as well as technical capacities to prepare and respond to disaster emergencies.

 

  1. Task 4: Build the capacity of the COP through consultative engagement: The consultant firm will foster the engagement of the community of practice established through this initiative (RCRP+) and establish a modality of communication between the COP members. This will include the development and implementation of a communication strategy.

  1. Training delivery

The delivery of the assignment will be led by a team of consultants (details in the Annex) under the guidance and with the support of the AUC.

 

  1. Designated Account

Upon completion, participants and their respective institutions are expected to achieve the following:

 

  1. Shared Understanding and Operational Mechanisms for Early Warning and Early Action:
    1. Establish a common operational understanding across hydromet, DRM, and regional institutions on multi-hazard early warning systems (MHEWS) and AMHEWAS.
    2. Consistently utilize hydrometeorological data, aligned with national and regional systems, to improve forecast accuracy and regional coherence.
    3. Apply standardized operational procedures (SOPs) for data exchange, warning generation, and coordination between national and regional actors.
    4. Strengthening integration of global observation systems and national forecasting workflows into routine operational practice.

 

  1. Operationalization of Early Action and Enhanced Preparedness:
    1. Demonstrate the capacity to interpret early warning information and translate it into timely, impact-based early actions at national and sub-national levels.
    2. Apply forecast-to-action frameworks, linking early warnings to predefined triggers, contingency plans, and sectoral responses.
    3. Improve coordination between hydromet agencies and disaster risk management institutions to enable timely, anticipatory decision-making.
    4. Strengthening the use of risk-informed decision support tools to reduce loss of life, livelihoods, and infrastructure damage during climate shocks.

 

  1. Sustained Regional Collaboration and Functioning Community of Practice
    1. Establish and operationalize a functional Community of Practice (COP) connecting RCRP-2 countries, AU, SADC, ICPAC, and other regional centers.
    2. Facilitate regular knowledge exchange and peer learning, including sharing of good practices, tools, and lessons learned.
    3. Promote regional collaboration and replication of successful approaches, ensuring sustained capacity development beyond the training program.

 

  1. Strengthened Capacity Base and Sustainability of Training Efforts
    1. Develop a COP of trained facilitators capable of delivering and adapting training at national and regional levels.
    2. Institutionalize training materials, tools, and methodologies within participating agencies to support continuous professional development.

 

  1. Potential Measurable Indicators
    1. ≥70–80% of participants demonstrate improved knowledge (pre/post training).
    2. At least 1–2 operational SOPs or coordination workflows adopted or refined per participating country.
    3. Onward training - Each trained facilitator trains minimum 1-2 additional persons in their country/institution.
    4. Evidence of early action triggered using forecast information in at least one case during the 6-month period.

 

  1. Target countries

The training programme will target RCRP 2 plus countries which are Malawi, Comoros, Madagascar, Mozambique and South Sudan. Apart from RCRP countries, additional Member States may be selected, with a geographical focus on countries in Africa East and South, with priority being given to Member States that have already established, are planning, or are in the process of establishing MHEWS Situation Rooms. The COP would also include representatives of SADC as well as other regional institutions such as ICPAC/IGAD, Eastern Nile Technical Regional Office (ENTRO), RCCs, and RSMCs.

 

  1. Module description

The scope of the training programme will focus on the following core modules:

Module 1: Hydromet services and integrated EWS.

Module 2: Disaster preparedness and Early Action.

Module 3: Climate Science and forecasting.

Module 4: Short term training AMHEWAS experts on data and Earth Observation.

Proposed training modules;

 

Module

Key focus areas

Profile of participants

Module 1:

Hydromet services and integrated EWS.

Target multi-sectoral participants including data/information generators and users.

 

Topics include:

  • Principles of data exchange and sharing in the context multi-hazard risk knowledge.
  • Interpretation of climate prediction and linking weather forecast to user confidence, effective early warning systems components,
  • Interpretation of floods and drought monitoring and early warning models and other available models.
  • Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) components.
  • Integrating exposure, vulnerability for impact-based forecasting and warning services.
  • Translating technical EW outputs into simplified risk communication (effective dissemination and communication).

This module will target experts from NDMAs and NHMAs with the following profile:

 

Degree holders from reputable institutions with at least 3 to 10 years of work experience

 

Managing situation rooms/ emergency operating centres

 

Demonstrated experience in data management, weather forecasting, climate prediction and multi-hazard early warning systems

 

Experience in risk mapping, GIS and vulnerability assessments

 

Experience in translating technical EW outputs into simplified risk communication (effective dissemination and communication)

 

Module 2:

Disaster preparedness and Early Action.

Focus on DRM and sectoral users (agriculture and livestock, energy, transport and water etc)

 

Topics include:

  • Developing and using multi-hazard risk assessments for sectoral planning
  • Anticipatory action (pre-arranged financing, triggers and thresholds)

Annexes

 

Annex 1: Roles and responsibilities

 

Introduction:

 

The AUC AMHEWAS recognizes the distinct roles and responsibilities of NDMAs, NMHSs and other stakeholders at continental, regional and national levels. The mandate for hydrological and weather observation, monitoring, forecasting and analyses at national level lies with the meteorological and hydrological agencies respectively depending on the national context. The NDMAs are basically users of the products provided by NMHSs. The AUC AMHEWAS simply aggregates regional guidance products from Regional Climate Centres and RSMCs, and make them available to Member States to have a synoptic analysis of Transboundary Risks. AMHEWAS does not produce early warnings and forecasts but aggregates information from national level to provide guidance to Member States for Anticipatory Action and further analytics. The AMHEWAS in respect to this training is to bring the services providers and the users on board to narrow the gap between early warning and anticipatory action. The involvement of RCC that are responsible for climate information and the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres (RSMC), Pretoria and RSMC La Reunion is to build regional and national capacities against severe weather and tropical cyclones. Their involvement in the training will help RCPR-2 countries to understand regional capacities, utility and services provided by these institutions. The goal of the AMHEWAS is if all member states are equipped with AMHEWAS situation rooms, the role of the AUC AMHEWAS will be simply to aggregate the information from the national and regional level to support the Civil Protection Mechanism and higher-level response. This approach seeks to enhance co-creation, co-designing, co-production and interoperability of multi-hazard early warning systems.

 

AU AMHEWAS will play the following roles and responsibilities:

 

  1. Support the consultants with the organisation of a series of training courses for the consultants and support the validation of the training materials.
  2. The AU will be responsible for the convening of the training. This will include logistical and administrative arrangements for the participants. The AU AMHEWAS team will support the consultants with relevant materials. 
  3. Provide overall coordination and stakeholder engagement for the training programme, including liaising with NDMAs, NMHSs, water authorities and other relevant institutions; coordinating participant nominations and official communications; facilitating consultations between consultants and national focal points; consolidating feedback on training materials; and ensuring that training activities are aligned with AMHEWAS objectives and country needs.

Republic of Uganda

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

COUNTRY: UGANDA

PROJECT: UGANDA LEARNING ACCELERATION PROGRAM (U-LEARN)

CREDIT NO. 7779-UG and GRANT NO.: C8807

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO UNDERTAKE INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION OF PROJECT RESULTS UNDER THE UGANDA LEARNING ACCELERATION PROGRAM (U-LEARN)

REFERENCE NO. MOES-ULEARN/SRVCS/2026-2027/00011

DATE OF ISSUANCE OF REOI: 23rd September 2026

The Government of the Republic of Uganda through the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) has received financing from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Uganda Learning Acceleration Program (ULEARN), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for hire of an Independent Verification Agent (IVA) to conduct independent verification of results for the Uganda Learning Acceleration Program (ULEARN).

The consulting services (“the Services”) include; (i) Conducting independent verification of the achievement of all eligible Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) and Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs) under ULEARN, (ii) Verification of results across the program implementation period, including document reviews, field verification, validation of reported data, assessment of compliance with agreed verification protocols, and confirmation of the achievement of results in accordance with the Financing Agreement, Programme Appraisal Document (PAD), Verification Protocol, and Project Operations Manual (POM).

The verification shall cover all implementing entities, beneficiary institutions, and geographic locations relevant to the DLIs being assessed. The IVA shall produce independent verification reports that confirm the extent to which the DLRs have been achieved. These reports shall provide a direct basis for the World Bank's assessment of DLR achievement and the corresponding disbursement recommendations under the Program.

The Independent Verification Agent (IVA) shall be engaged for the duration of the ULEARN Program implementation, expected to until run 30th June 2030 subject to satisfactory performance, continued need for the services, and availability of funding.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.education.go.ug or can be obtained at the address given below.

The Ministry of Education and Sports now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

The firm shall meet the following minimum requirements:

  1. At least ten (10) years of demonstrated experience in conducting independent verification, performance audits, Program evaluations for Government institutions.
  2. Demonstrated experience in at least three (3) assignments involving verification or evaluation of large-scale education, infrastructure, or public sector Programs within the last ten (10) years.
  3. Proven experience in verifying results under Results-Based Financing (RBF), Program-for-Results (PforR), Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs), or similar performance-based financing mechanisms is highly desirable.
  4. Experience working on projects financed by the World Bank, African Development Bank, or other multilateral development partners will be an added advantage.
  5. Demonstrated capacity to deploy a multidisciplinary team comprising experts in education, engineering, procurement, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, monitoring and evaluation, Information and Technology and data management. (Please do not submit CVs and bio data of experts).
  6. Capacity to undertake nationwide field verification and quality assurance.
  7. Demonstrated experience in the use of digital data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, GEMS, ODK, Survey123, or equivalent) capable of capturing geo-tagged photographs, GPS coordinates, and date/time stamps.
  8. Experience implementing similar assignments in Uganda or the East African region or Sub-Saharan Africa will be an added advantage.
  9. Demonstrate high standards of professional integrity, independence, confidentiality, and quality assurance, and shall have no actual or perceived conflict of interest in relation to the implementation of ULEARN

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, and should indicate clearly in the Expression of Interest (EOI) whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (Monday to Friday, 09:00 – 17:00 hours, except on public holidays).

REPUBLIC OF TÜRKYE

MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, URBANIZATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE (MOEUCC)

GENERAL DIRECTORATE of CONSTRUCTION AFFAIRS (GDCA)

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION-LCS)

 

TÜRKYE SECOND ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN PUBLIC BUILDINGS PROJECT

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR

ENERGY AUDIT, DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION SERVICES FOR ENERGY EFFICIENCY RENOVATIONS IN PUBLIC BUILDINGS IN SAMSUN

Reference No:

(EEPB2/WB/MoEUCC/LCS-DES&SUP-02)

This request for expressions of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this project that appeared in UNDB on December 17, 2024 with reference no WB 8227-07/19.

The Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Second Energy Efficiency in Public Buildings Project (EEPBP2) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The General Directorate of Construction Affairs (“GDCA”) of the Ministry of Environment Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change (MoEUCC) serves as the main implementing agency for the Project. A project implementation unit (PIU) has been established under GDCA to manage the activities related to the Project. The overall objective of EEPBP2 to reduce energy use in central government buildings and develop a transition plan to develop and scale-up suitable sustainable financing and institutional mechanisms to support a national program. The implementation period for the project is planned as 6 years.

Table 1 indicates the tasks to be provided under the scope of the consulting services (“the Services”).

Table 1: The Consultant’s Services

 

Task No

Services to be provided for the subprojects given in Table 2 as specified in Terms of Reference (ToR)

Task I

1

Conduct investment grade energy audits of below-listed public buildings to combine solar PV investments with investments in light-emitting diode (LED) to replace inefficient lighting technologies and electrification of heating (i.e., substituting fossil-fuel boiler capacity with heat pumps to support both heating and cooling) according to the energy audit report template and prepare full detailed audit reports

2

Prepare detailed designs and technical specifications including BOQs and cost estimates for energy efficiency renovations in below-listed public buildings based on detailed energy audit reports, local laws/standards/regulations

3

Identify environmental and social risks associated with the building renovations and prepare Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) for each building site

4

Assist the PIU on preparation of bidding documents, clarifications, amendments, updating cost estimates, etc. until construction contract award

Task II

5

Carry out construction supervision and building commissioning services, ensure adherence to ESMPs, local laws/regulations and building commissioning

6

Supervise any remedial works to rectify defects that arise during the Defects Notification Period (DNP)

7

Conduct Measurement and Verification (M&V) over a period of 12 months, under the Supervision Contract

The detailed Terms of References (TORs) for the Services can be found at the following web page address: https://www.kabev.org/ihale-ilanlari/

The General Directorate of Construction Affairs (GDCA) now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The selection criteria for the short-listing are:

The Consultants should be in the consulting business for not less than the last 10 years prior to deadline for submission of interests

The Consultants should have at least 5 years of similar experience prior to deadline for submission of interests in the Services listed in Table 1,

The Consultants should demonstrate sound administrative and financial capacity

The Consultants should demonstrate availability of the key experts for the performance of the services described in the TOR;

Note: Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Note: GDCA reserves sole right to request Consultant for verification of any submitted document/information in accordance with the applicable Law.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s dated September 2023 “Procurement Regulations” setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest (https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/6c0602876d68949e80820507d90a14ed-0290012023/original/Procurement-Regulations-September-2023.pdf).

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture should have a legal entity and shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Interested consultants should clearly indicate the structure of their “association” and the duties of the partners and sub-consultants in their application. Unclear expression of interests in terms of “in association with” and/or “in affiliation with” and etc. may not be evaluated. Consultants shall submit only one EOI either individually as a single consultant or as a partner in a joint venture. Consultants may associate with more than one firm or joint venture in the capacity of a sub-consultant. No firm can be a sub-consultant while submitting an EOI individually as a firm or as a partner of a joint venture. Sub-consultants’ experience will not contribute in evaluating the experience of the interested single consultant or joint venture. Sub-consultants’ qualifications and experience will only be considered in evaluating the personnel capacity of the interested single consultant or joint venture.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Least Cost Selection (LCS) method described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

N° MSP/ PPRRUS/AMI/17/2026

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

REPUBLIQUE DU BURUNDI

PROJET DE PREPARATION, DE REPONSE ET DE RESILIENCE AUX URGENCES SANITAIRES (PPRRUS) AU BURUNDI

Recrutement d’un bureau d’études en vue de la Réalisation des Etudes Techniques, le Contrôle et la Surveillance des Travaux relatifs à (a) la Réhabilitation du Laboratoire National Vétérinaire (LABVET) et (b) la Construction d’un Bâtiment de bureaux pour le Centre des Opérations d’Urgence de la Santé Publique (COUSP)

N° de référence (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés): BI-MOH-544140-CS-CQS

Le Gouvernement du Burundi/ Ministère de la Santé Publique a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Préparation, de Réponse et de Résilience aux Urgences Sanitaires (PPRRUS) au Burundi, et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : recrutement d’un bureau d’ étude en vue de la Réalisation des Etudes Techniques, le Contrôle et la Surveillance des Travaux relatifs à  (a) la Réhabilitation du Laboratoire National Vétérinaire (LABVET) et (b) la Construction d’un Bâtiment de bureaux pour le Centre des Opérations d’Urgence de la Santé Publique (COUSP).

Les services de consultants (« les services ») comprennent (i) les services d'ingénierie, de conception détaillée et (ii) de contrôle et de surveillance des travaux pour deux infrastructures distinctes situées au centre-ville de Bujumbura, à savoir :

  1. La Réhabilitation du Laboratoire National Vétérinaire (LABVET), intervention sur un bâtiment existant nécessitant une remise aux normes structurelles, fonctionnelles et réglementaires, afin de renforcer les capacités nationales de diagnostic vétérinaire et de surveillance des maladies zoonotiques ; et
  2. La Construction et l'aménagement des locaux du Centre des Opérations d'Urgence de Santé Publique (COUSP) : conception et réalisation d'un nouveau bâtiment destiné à abriter le dispositif national de coordination et de réponse aux urgences sanitaires.

Ces deux (2) infrastructures, bien que complémentaires dans leurs objectifs, requièrent des approches techniques distinctes : l'une portant sur la réhabilitation et la mise aux normes d'un ouvrage existant, l'autre sur la conception et la construction d'un ouvrage neuf. Le bureau d'études devra en tenir compte à chaque étape de son exécution.

Les services d'ingénierie et de conception détaillée sont estimés à 195 hommes- jours tandis que le temps de   contrôle et de surveillance des travaux pour les deux infrastructures est estimé à 8 mois.  Le début de la mission est prévu au mois de janvier 2029. 

Les termes de référence détaillés (TdR) pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

Le Ministère de la Santé Publique/ Projet de Préparation, de Réponse et de Résilience aux Urgences Sanitaires (PPRRUS) au Burundi invite maintenant les cabinets de consultants éligibles ("Consultants") à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

  1. Avoir au moins 10 ans d’expérience dans l’exécution des études des travaux et de Surveillance.
  2. Avoir réalisé au moins trois (3) marchés en matière d’étude et de surveillance liée aux bâtiments de même complexité,
  3. Avoir réalisé au moins un (1) marché en matière d’étude et de surveillance liée aux bâtiments hospitaliers ou laboratoires, en particulier les laboratoires vétérinaires pour les cinq dernières années constituerait un atout majeur. Les bâtiments des personnels privés ne seront pas considérés,
  4. Avoir réalisé une (1) mission dans le Cadre Environnemental et Social de la Banque Mondiale (ESF), les normes de santé et sécurité au travail (SST), et les codes nationaux applicables à la construction et à l’exploitation de laboratoires, selon les exigences du projet.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués au stade de la présélection.

La liste restreinte sera composée d'un cabinet.

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions de la section III, paragraphe 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’Investissement (FPI), version de septembre 2023 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts. 

Les consultants peuvent s'associer à d'autres firmes pour renforcer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l'association prend la forme d'une coentreprise et/ou d'une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d'une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de l'intégralité du contrat, s'ils sont sélectionnés.

Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur les Qualifications du consultant (SFQ) énoncée dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau c'est-à-dire de 07h30 à 15h30.

Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être remises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous en personne, ou par e-mail, au plus tard le 22/10/2026 à 10 heures, heures locales

AVIS DE DEMANDE DE COTATION

N°029 /DC/MINDDEVEL/PROLOG/UGP/SPM/2026 DU 02 SEPTEMBRE 2026

RELATIVE A L’ACQUISITION ET L’INSTALLATION DU MATERIEL DE SECURITE ET INCENDIE, ET PREMIERS SECOURS POUR L'UGP ET LES 06 UCR DU PROJET GOUVERNANCE LOCALE ET COMMUNAUTES RESILIENTES (PROLOG) 

 

Le Gouvernement du Cameroun a obtenu l’assistance technique et financière de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) à travers la Banque mondiale afin de mener à bien l’exécution du Projet Gouvernance Locale et Communautés Résilientes (PROLOG), et se propose d’utiliser une partie des fonds du crédit IDA N°72130-CM pour effectuer des paiements autorisés au titre du Contrat pour lequel cette Demande de Cotation est publiée.

Le Coordonnateur du Projet Gouvernance Locale et Communautés Résilientes (PROLOG) invite les Fournisseurs intéressés, à soumettre leurs offres sous pli fermé, en vue de « l’Acquisition et l’installation du matériel de sécurité et incendie, et premiers secours pour l'UGP et les 06 UCR du Projet Gouvernance Locale et Communautés Résilientes (PROLOG) ».

 

Le dossier de Demande de Cotation est à retirer gratuitement dans les locaux de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet Gouvernance Locale et Communautés Résilientes (PROLOG), sise au 2ème étage de l’immeuble rose – saumon en vitres, situé avant l’Agence de Régulation des Marchés Publics (ARMP), au quartier dit Dragages, Yaoundé – Cameroun, aux heures ouvrables, par voie électronique aux adresses mentionnées ci-dessous.

Les offres rédigées en français ou en anglais, en sept (07) exemplaires (dont un (01) original et six (06) copies, marqués comme tels et avec une copie numérique sur CD ou clef USB seront chiffrées hors TVA (HT) et toutes taxes comprises (TTC) et accompagnées du modèle de la Lettre de marché signé, qui constituera le contrat au cas où l’offre serait retenue.

Les offres seront déposées au plus tard quatorze (14) jours à compter de la date de publication du présent avis dans le Journal des Marchés de l’ARMP», soit le 18 Septembre 2026 à 14 heures précises (heure locale), à l’Unité de Gestion du Projet Gouvernance Locale et Communautés Résilientes (PROLOG), sise au 2ème étage de l’immeuble rose – saumon en vitres, situé avant l’Agence de Régulation des Marchés Publics (ARMP), au quartier dit Dragages, Yaoundé – Cameroun, et devront porter la mention :

« DEMANDE DE COTATION

N°029/DC/MINDDEVEL/PROLOG/UGP/CSPM/2026 DU 02 SEPTEMBRE 2026

POUR L’ACQUISITION ET L’INSTALLATION DU MATERIEL DE SECURITE ET INCENDIE, ET PREMIERS SECOURS POUR L'UGP ET LES 06 UCR DU PROJET GOUVERNANCE LOCALE ET COMMUNAUTES RESILIENTES (PROLOG).

A N’OUVRIR QU’EN SEANCE DE DEPOUILLEMENT. »

NB : La soumission des offres par voie électronique n’est pas autorisée.

Les plis seront ouverts quatorze (14) jours à compter de la date de publication du présent avis dans le Journal des Marchés de l’ARMP, soit le 18 Septembre 2026

 à 15 heures (heure locale), par la Commission Spéciale de Passation des Marchés placée auprès du PROLOG, sise au 1er étage de l’immeuble rose – saumon en vitres, situé avant l’Agence de Régulation des Marchés Publics (ARMP), au quartier dit Dragages, Yaoundé – Cameroun, en présence des soumissionnaires ou de leurs représentants dûment mandatés.

Les offres resteront valables pendant soixante (60) jours à partir de la date d’ouverture des plis.

L’Acheteur attribuera le marché au soumissionnaire, dont il aura déterminé que l’offre est conforme pour l’essentiel aux dispositions du Dossier de Demande de Cotations, et qu’elle est la cotation la « moins – disante », à condition que le Soumissionnaire soit en outre jugé qualifié pour exécuter le Marché de façon satisfaisante selon les conditions suivantes :

Le soumissionnaire doit prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences d’expérience ci-après :

  • Justifie d’un marché/contrat/prestation similaire (joindre la première et la page de signature du contrat/marché/prestation), réalisé par le soumissionnaire en tant que fournisseur principal au cours des cinq (07) dernières années, assorti de PV, la nature des fournitures doit être produite avec les montants en monnaie librement convertible (HT et TTC) et les noms des Acheteurs ;
  • Possède un dossier administratif (voir 5.4 de la Demande de cotation) en cours de validité.

Le délai de livraison est de trente (30) jours.

L’Unité de Gestion du Projet Gouvernance Locale et Communautés Résilientes (PROLOG), sise au 2ème étage de l’immeuble rose – saumon en vitres, situé avant l’Agence de Régulation des Marchés Publics (ARMP), au quartier dit Dragages, Yaoundé – Cameroun.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Georgia

KAKHETI CONNECTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT 

Project ID: P173782

Loan No: 9361-GE

Assignment Title: International Bridge/Structural Engineer

Reference No. KCIP/CS/ICS-04R

The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kakheti Connectivity Improvement Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI) now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the following services: International Bridge/Structural Engineer. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The CVs of the candidates should cover the requested information.

The International Bridge/Structural Engineer will assist the RDMRDI to ensure that all bridge and structural components under ongoing and planned road projects are designed, constructed, and maintained in compliance with relevant technical regulations, engineering standards, and Georgian laws as well as meet the requirements set forth by the World Bank and other international best practices. This role involves close daily collaboration with RD and encompasses tasks such as preparing road designs, supervising construction activities, coordinating site visits, and other related duties.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/k6qlc77hzt2hhnyps1jcz/TOR-of-Bridge-Engineer-04R.pdf?rlkey=8mquw6qfnmmjv3eza642vq8su&dl=0

The Qualification Requirements for selection of the Consultant are as follows:

  • Master’s Degree or equivalent in Civil Engineering preferably with specialization in bridge/structural engineering with at least 8 years of experience in the road projects on a position of Bridge/structural Engineer;
  • Minimum of 5 years of international experience in road construction/reconstruction/rehabilitation and/or construction supervision assignments on a similar position;
  • Proven experience in preparing design documentation and/or design review assignments for highways and related infrastructure;
  • Experience of working in institutional and physical environments similar to those prevailing;
  • Familiarity with national and international bridge design standards (e.g., AASHTO, Eurocode, DIN);
  • Ability to utilize and share knowledge and best international practices to benefit works contractors and supervisions consultants;
  • Ability to work both independently and within teams;
  • Possess superior verbal and writing communication skills in English language.

The period of the consultancy services shall be 24 months (with possibility of downstream extension, subject to satisfactory performance) and the remuneration will be time-based.

Note: The Road Department reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The consultant shall not receive any payment in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the Client under the contract.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address: info@georoad.ge.

 

Expressions of Interest accompanied by CVs and other relevant information electronically or in printed materials must be delivered to the address below not later than October 30, 2026, 18:00 hours.

 

The Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI).

Attn: Ms. Salome Tsurtsumia, Deputy Chairperson

12 Al. Kazbegi Avenue, Tbilisi, 0160, Georgia

Tel: (995 32) 2 37-05-08

Email: info@georoad.ge

procnotices.contact_address: Ministère du Plan
procnotices.notice_text:
AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET N° 02/MEPSP/2026/UGP PRACAC

 

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D'UNE ONG LOCALE SPECIALISEE DANS LA PREVENTION ET LA REPONSE AUX VIOLENCES BASEES SUR LE GENRE (VBG), Y COMPRIS L'EXPLOITATION ET LES ABUS SEXUELS (EAS) ET LE HARCELEMENT SEXUEL (HS) ET CHARGEE DE LA FORMATION, DE LA COMMUNICATION SOCIALE, DU SOUTIEN PSYCHOSOCIAL AINSI QUE DE LA SENSIBILISATION ET DE LA VULGARISATION DU MECANISME DE GESTION DES PLAINTES (MGP) DU PRACAC

 

  1. Les Gouvernements de la République du Congo et de la République Centrafricaine ont signé avec la Banque Mondiale respectivement un accord de prêt et un accord de don pour un montant total de 330 millions USD, dont 90 millions USD pour la République du Congo et 240 millions USD pour la République Centrafricaine pour la mise en œuvre du Projet Régional d'Amélioration des Corridors de Transport Routier et Fluvial en Afrique centrale (PRACAC). L’Unité de Gestion de Projet (UGP) de la République du Congo a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Recrutement d'une ONG locale spécialisée dans la prévention et la réponse aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG), y compris l'exploitation et les abus sexuels (EAS) et le harcèlement sexuel (HS), chargée de la formation, de la communication sociale, du soutien psychosocial ainsi que de la sensibilisation et de la vulgarisation du mécanisme de gestion des plaintes (MGP) DU PRACAC ».
  2. L'objectif général de la mission est de prévenir, d'atténuer et de répondre aux risques de VBG/EAS/HS liés à la mise en œuvre du projet, d'une part, et de contribuer au fonctionnement du Mécanisme de Gestion des Plaintes (MGP) du PRACAC, d'autre part, conformément aux exigences du Cadre Environnemental et Social de la Banque mondiale.
  3. Le présent avis à manifestation d’intérêt vise à identifier des ONG locales pour faire partie de la liste restreinte en vue de la consultation relative à ladite mission.
  4. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet, invite les ONG éligibles, à manifester leur intérêt et à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les ONG intéressées peuvent s’associer avec d’autres ONG locales spécialisées dans le domaine du marché pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives. Elles doivent fournir les informations ci-après : (i) qualification pour exécuter les services sollicités (références et descriptions concernant l’exécution de missions similaires, brochures…) ; (ii) les capacités techniques de l’ONG, les domaines d’intervention ainsi que les années d’expérience de l’ONG, les références des clients bénéficiaires des prestations décrites.
  5. Les critères pour l'évaluation des Manifestations d’Intérêt sont les suivants : (i) les qualifications générales et expérience de l’ONG locale dans le domaine de la mission, (ii) l'expérience de l’ONG locale dans la réalisation de missions similaires.
  6. L'attention des candidats intéressés est attirée sur le fait que, les ONG sollicitées devront spécifiquement être des ONG locales spécialisées et ayant de l’expérience dans le domaine de la mission en objet.
  7. L’ONG sera sélectionnée selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualification de Consultants (SQC) tel que défini dans le Règlement de Passation de Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) de la Banque Mondiale, Edition de septembre 2025.
  8. Les ONG intéressées peuvent obtenir les termes de référence ou des informations supplémentaires aux adresses indiquées ci-dessous de 9h00 à 12h00 et de 14h00 à 16h00 (heure locale).
  9. Les manifestations d’intérêts portant la mention : « Recrutement d'une ONG locale spécialisée dans la prévention et la réponse aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG), y compris l'exploitation et les abus sexuels (EAS) et le harcèlement sexuel (HS), chargée de la formation, de la communication sociale, du soutien psychosocial ainsi que de la sensibilisation et de la vulgarisation du mécanisme de gestion des plaintes (MGP) DU PRACAC » doivent être envoyées au plus tard le 09 octobre 2026 à 16 heures (heure locale) aux adresses ci-dessous :

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

Georgia

KAKHETI CONNECTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT 

Project ID: P173782

Loan No: 9361-GE

Assignment Title: International Pavement Engineer

Reference No. KCIP/CS/ICS-07R

The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kakheti Connectivity Improvement Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI) now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the following services: International Pavement Engineer. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The CVs of the candidates should cover the requested information.

The International Pavement Engineer will review and verify pavement designs in line with IFI guidelines, FIDIC conditions, and international standards; assess material suitability and performance; supervise construction to ensure quality compliance; analyze test results; and provide technical recommendations. The Engineer will also prepare technical reports, support payment certificates and variation orders, and coordinate with the RD, consultants, contractors, and stakeholders through regular field monitoring and coordination meetings, ensuring adherence to industry best practices.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/y0h6zx8w6i5d3f2h23pi4/TOR-Pavement-Engineer-07R.pdf?rlkey=fl3e1l6gyvhecwlwy1749ndnr&dl=0

The Qualification Requirements for selection of the Consultant are as follows:

  • Master’s degree or equivalent, in Civil Engineering, preferably in Pavement Engineering, Transportation Engineering, or Materials Engineering with 8 years of experience in road sector on a similar position;
  • Preferably 5 years of relevant professional International experience in pavement design, materials evaluation in design/construction/reconstruction/rehabilitation and/or construction supervision for road infrastructure projects, including significant experience in working on MDB-funded projects in sensitive environments;
  • Familiarity with international standards such as AASHTO, ASTM, EN for roads and highways;
  • Experience of working in institutional and physical environments similar to those prevailing;
  • Ability to utilize and share knowledge and best international practices to benefit works contractors and supervisions consultants;
  • Ability to work both independently and within teams.
  • Possess superior verbal and writing communication skills in English language.

The period of the consultancy services shall be 24 months (with possibility of downstream extension, subject to satisfactory performance) and the remuneration will be time-based.

Note: The Road Department reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”,  Seventh Edition,  September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The consultant shall not receive any payment in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the Client under the contract.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address: info@georoad.ge.

Expressions of Interest accompanied by CVs and other relevant information electronically or in printed materials must be delivered to the address below not later than October 30, 2026, 18:00 hours.

The Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI).

ENMIENDA  AL LLAMADO DE LA SOLICITUD DE PROPUESTAS

Llamado de la Solicitud de Propuestas

Solicitud de Propuestas para Obras

(Diseño y Construcción)

 

Contratante: Secretaría de Agricultura y Ganadería (SAG).

Proyecto: Proyecto de Seguridad Hídrica en el Corredor Seco de Honduras.

Nombre del contrato: Diseño y Rehabilitación de la Planta de Tratamiento de Agua Potable de Nacaome, (PTAP Nacaome).

País: Honduras.

Crédito No.: 6680-HN.

SDP No.: SDP-O-1-SH-6680-2026.

Solicitud de Propuestas No.: STEP, HN-SAG-553515-CW-RFP.

Emitida el: Doce (12) de agosto de 2026.

1. El Gobierno de la República de Honduras ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo de Proyecto de Seguridad Hídrica en el Corredor Seco de Honduras, y tiene la intención de aplicar una parte de los fondos obtenidos para realizar pagos en virtud del contrato correspondiente al Diseño y Rehabilitación de la Planta de Tratamiento de Agua Potable de Nacaome, (PTAP Nacaome).

2. La Secretaría de Agricultura y Ganadería (SAG), a través de la Unidad de Administración de Proyectos (UAP) y Unidad de Gestión de Proyecto (UGP) del Proyecto de Seguridad Hídrica en el Corredor Seco de Honduras, invita a los Proponentes elegibles a presentar Propuestas en sobre cerrado para El Diseño y Rehabilitación de la Planta de Tratamiento de Agua Potable de Nacaome, (PTAP Nacaome). Cuya capacidad es de 72 L/s. El proyecto se encuentra ubicado en las siguientes coordenadas, Zona 16P (13.529722, -87.485278) y tiene contemplado los siguiente: 

  • Sectores a intervenir: Plan de Gestión Ambiental y Social del Contratista (PGAS-C), azud, bombeo, pretratamiento, floculación y sedimentación, sistemas eléctricos y de automatización, dosificación química, filtración, tanques, lodos, equipamiento electromecánico, laboratorio, energía solar y obras arquitectónicas. 
  • Componentes a rehabilitar: Sistemas hidráulicos y de proceso, dosificación química, mejoras eléctricas y de infraestructura.
  • Componentes nuevos: Hidrociclones de desarenado, migración a hipoclorito de calcio e insumo para ajuste de pH, automatización, sistema solar y cisterna de almacenamiento.
  • Particularidad de la Planta de Nacaome: Instalación de una nueva línea de floculación y sedimentación. La rehabilitación se ejecutará manteniendo la planta en operación continua[1], sin interrupción del servicio.
  • Período de Entrega/Construcción es: Once (11) meses.

3. REPUBLIQUE DU SENEGAL

UN PEUPLE – UN BUT – UNE FOI

------------

 

 

 

 

 

PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES A L’ELECTRICITE AU SENEGAL (PADAES)

 

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET – AMI N°35/2026

 

PAYS : SENEGAL

PROJET : PROJET D’AMELIORATION DE L’ACCES A L’ELECTRICITE AU SENEGAL (PADAES)

Coût Financement Crédit/Prêt du Projet : 150 000 000 USD$

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT POUR LA REALISATION DES ETUDES APS, APD, POUR L’ELECTRIFICATION A MOINDRE COÛT DES LOCALITES DANS LE PERIMETRE DE SENELEC

 

N° Projet : P176620             

N° de Crédits IDA : 70470-SN et 8066-SN

N° de Référence PPM Banque Mondiale : 34-CONS-PADAES-2026

N° de Référence PPM SENELEC 2022 : C_PADAES_338

1. Cette sollicitation de manifestations d’intérêt (MI) fait suite à l’Avis Général de Passation des Marchés publié dans le système STEP de la Banque mondiale, puis dans United Nations Development Business (UNDB) Online, sous la référence publiée le 29 mars 2022, ainsi qu’à la publication nationale parue dans le quotidien Le Soleil N° 16668 des mercredi 24 et jeudi 25 décembre 2025.

2. L’État du Sénégal a reçu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des ressources de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat portant sur le :

« Recrutement d’un consultant pour la réalisation des études d’Avant-Projet Sommaire (APS), d’Avant-Projet Détaillé (APD), pour l’électrification à moindre coût des Localités situées dans le périmètre de SENELEC. »

3. OBJECTIF DE LA MISSION :

L’objectif global de la mission est de recruter un consultant chargé de réaliser l’étude de faisabilité de l’électrification des localités situées dans le périmètre de Senelec et éligibles à une électrification par extension du réseau moyenne tension.

 A cet effet, le consultant sera chargé de réaliser les prestations suivantes :

  • La réalisation des études techniques d’Avant-Projet Sommaire (APS) et d’Avant-Projet Détaillé (APD) ;
  • L’analyse économique et financière du projet ;
  • La réalisation des études environnementales et sociales (EIES/AEI), y compris l’élaboration des Plans de Réinstallation (PR), le cas échéant ;
  • L’élaboration du dossier d’appel d’offres (DAO) en vue de la réalisation des travaux.

De manière spécifique, il est attendu du consultant qu’il propose une méthodologie claire, cohérente et optimisée permettant la réalisation, à moindre coût, des études de faisabilité relatives à l’électrification des localités concernées, ainsi que l’élaboration du dossier d’appel d’offres.

Les objectifs spécifiques de la mission sont les suivants :

  • Déterminer, pour chaque localité, le tracé de raccordement optimal au réseau moyenne tension afin de minimiser les pertes techniques et d’optimiser les coûts d’investissement ;
  • Évaluer les investissements nécessaires à l’électrification de l’ensemble des clients potentiels situés dans la zone d’étude ;
  • Proposer un calendrier réaliste de mise en œuvre des travaux ;
  • Élaborer les instruments de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale (EIES, AEI et Plans de Réinstallation), sur la base des résultats du screening environnemental et social ;
  • Analyser les impacts environnementaux et sociaux potentiels du projet et proposer des mesures d’atténuation conformes à la réglementation nationale ainsi qu’aux exigences applicables de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Élaborer le dossier d’appel d’offres (DAO) destiné à la passation des marchés de travaux.

Le consultant devra mobiliser toutes les compétences, ressources humaines et moyens matériels nécessaires à la bonne exécution de la mission et à l’atteinte des objectifs fixés.

4. DESCRIPTION DU PROJET :

 

Pour soutenir l’ambition nationale d’atteindre l’accès universel à l’électricité d’ici 2029, la SENELEC, avec l’appui de ses partenaires au développement, a engagé des investissements stratégiques visant à moderniser et à étendre le réseau électrique national.

La présente étude portera sur les 1661 localités restantes, réparties comme indiqué dans le tableau ci-après :

Compte tenu de la répartition géographique des localités, illustrée par la figure ci-après, le périmètre de l’étude est subdivisé en deux (02) lots :

  • Lot 1 : Localités de la zone Centre-Ouest ;
  • Lot 2 : Localités de la zone Sud et Nord-Est.

 Le Consultant, la Firme ou le Groupement a la possibilité de soumissionner pour les deux (02) lots, en le précisant dans sa lettre de soumission. Toutefois, un même consultant ne pourra être attributaire que d’un seul (01) Lot.

Par ailleurs, un consultant ne peut être retenu simultanément à titre individuel et en qualité de membre d’un groupement. De même, un même consultant ne peut participer à plusieurs groupements.

Dans le cas où un consultant serait classé premier sur plus d’un lot, il lui sera attribué le lot présentant le linéaire HTA le plus important.

Tout consultant souhaitant soumissionner pour les deux (02) lots devra présenter deux propositions techniques distinctes et deux propositions financières distinctes. S’il choisit de soumissionner pour un seul lot, il devra clairement préciser le lot concerné dans son offre.

5. Qualification et Compétences du Consultant

                                                     

Le Consultant doit être un Cabinet ou Firme ou un Groupement et doit respecter les critères de préqualification ci-après :

                                      

  • Être un Consultant d’Etudes Techniques et Environnementales, intervenant dans le Secteur de l’Energie Electrique et de l’Environnement, avec une expérience avérée en électrification rurale, et détenir un agrément délivré par le Ministère de l’Environnement et de la Transition Ecologique du Sénégal pour la Réalisation d’Etudes Environnementales (en cas de Groupement au moins un des membres doit détenir cet agrément) ;
  • Disposer d’expérience d’au moins dix (10) ans dans le domaine de l’Electricité, et des Etudes Techniques des Réseaux de Distribution d’Electricité HTA et BT ;
  • Disposer d’une Expérience avérée dans la Conduite d’Etudes Environnementales et Sociales ;
  • Justifier avec des attestations de Bonne Exécution, la réalisation au cours des Quinze (15) dernières années (2010-2025) :
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Etude d’Avant-Projet Détaillée (APD) de taille similaire pour des Projets de Distribution d’Electricité HTA et BT;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Elaboration de Dossier d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) pour des Travaux de Réseaux de Distribution HTA et BT ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Evaluation Economique et Financière de Projet d’Electrification Rurale ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins de Mission d’Evaluation Environnementale et Sociale de Projet(s) d’Electrification Rurale financé par un Partenaire Technique Financier (PTF) comme la Banque Mondiale, l’AFD, la BEI, l’UE, la KfW, la BAD, etc. ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins en matière d’Elaboration de PR suivant la Réglementation Nationale en vigueur et la NES 5 de la Banque Mondiale ;
  • Une (01) Expérience au moins dans les Pays de la Sous-Région, Francophone.

 

  • Le Consultant doit aussi : 

                                                                                              

  • Détenir une Licence et justifier de la capacité d’utilisation d’un Logiciel spécialisé SIG ;
  • Détenir une Licence et justifier de la capacité d’utilisation d’un Logiciel de Planification.

NB : Le Consultant doit fournir des Attestations de Bonne Exécution ou de Services Faits pour chaque expérience annoncée. Les Contrats signés ne remplacent pas les Attestations de Bonne Exécution ou de Services Faits.

 

6. DUREE DE LA MISSION :

 

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission du Consultant est de Quinze (15) mois à partir de son Entrée en Vigueur marquée par la Notification du Contrat immatriculé au Consultant par Senelec et un (01) mois pour l’Elaboration du Rapport de Consolidation.

 

7. Les Consultants (Cabinet ou Firme ou Groupement), seront sélectionnés selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Cout (SFQC). Les Critères d’Eligibilité, l’établissement de la liste restreinte et la procédure de sélection seront conformes aux Règlements de la Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) des éditions référenciées au-dessus (Juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Août 2018, Novembre 2020 et en Février 2025) », applicable au Projet et les dispositions de la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement, relatives aux Règles de la Banque Mondiale en matière de Conflit d’Intérêts sont applicables.

 

8. Les Consultants (Cabinet ou Firme ou un Groupement) intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations en transmettant une demande à l’adresse ci-dessous, tous les jours ouvrables de 07 H 30 mn à 16 H 30 mn : Direction Passation des Marchés Senelec, sise, au 19 rue Abdou Karim Bourgi x Wagane Diouf au 2ème étage de la Résidence Khoudia - Dakar, Sénégal. Adresse électronique : notificationcpm@senelec.sn.

 

9. Les Manifestations d’Intérêt en français officiel doivent être soumises au plus tard le MERCREDI 21 octobre 2026 à 09 HEURES 30 MN PRECISES, HEURE LOCALE.

  • En Version Physique, dont un (01) original et trois (03) copies, déposées à Senelec Salle de la Commission des Marchés de Senelec sise au 19, Rue Abdou Karim Bourgi x Wagane Diouf au 2ème étage de la Résidence Khoudia, Dakar ;
  • Et en Version Electronique par courriel aux adresses suivantes :  notificationcpm@senelec.sn & mamearame.ndieguene@senelec.sn.

 

10. Les Consultants qui souhaitent déposer leurs manifestations d’intérêt avant la date d’ouverture des Manifestations d’Intérêt les remettront à la Direction Passation des Marchés, sise au 19 rue Abdou Karim Bourgi X Wagane Diouf au 2ème étage de la résidence Khoudia Dakar, tous les jours ouvrables de 07 H 30 mn à 16 H 30 mn. Les manifestations d’intérêt seront ouvertes à la même adresse en présence des représentants des candidats au plus tard le MERCREDI 21 octobre 2026 à 09 HEURES 30MN PRECISES.
