procnotices.notice_text:
Specific Procurement Notice

Request for Bids, Goods

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

Country: Georgia

Name of Project: Log-In Georgia

Contract Title: IP/MPLS Active Equipment, Phase 2

Loan No.: 9161-GE

RFB Reference No.: GE-OPEN NET-478181-GO-RFB-2

  1. Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Log-In Georgia Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for IP/MPLS Active Equipment, Phase 2. This contract will be jointly financed by EIB. Bidding process will be governed by the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.
  2. The N(N)LE Open Net now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for IP/MPLS Active Equipment, Phase 2. The Goods includes but not limited to the following items: aggregation routers, access devices, core routers, air conditioners, 48V power supplies SEP’s, environmental monitoring systems, NOC, firewalls of the quantities and specifications, and delivery term as per the Schedule of Requirements and Technical Specifications (Annex 1) of the Bidding Document. Installation and configuration of the Goods, as well as providing warranty are required and specified in the Bidding Document.  No margin of preference is applied.
  3. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB)  as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, 7th Edition (September, 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.
  4. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 30 %, and for Bid cost: 70 %. 
  5. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information and documents at “Georgian Electronic - Government Procurement System (GE-GP)” – the official portal of State Procurement in Georgia, operated by the State Procurement Agency (http://procurement.gov.ge/ ).
  6. The bidding document in English may be obtained by interested eligible Bidders at “Georgian Electronic - Government Procurement System (GE-GP)” (http://procurement.gov.ge/ ) in electronic format and can be downloaded for free at the link: https://tenders.procurement.gov.ge/public/?go=696751&lang=ge 
  7. Bids must be delivered electronically using “Georgian Electronic - Government Procurement System (GE-GP)”, (http://procurement.gov.ge/ ). Bids shall consist of two parts:  one file marked “Technical Part” of the Bid which shall consist of all the technical parameters of the bid, and the second file - encrypted (password-protected) pdf file marked “Financial Part” of the Bid, which shall combine all the financial forms and financial information of the Bid.  Late Bids will be rejected (shall not be accepted by the GE-GP system).  Bid price must not be indicated in the GE-GP system; instead, bid price field of the GE-GP system shall be filled in with the figure “1”. Bids will be opened electronically:

-  The file marked “Technical Part” of the Bid will be opened as it will be informed by GE-GP system and read-out.

- The encrypted file marked “Financial Part” of the Bid shall remain unopened: the opening date of “Financial Part” of the Bid will be not less than ten (10) Business Days from the date of notification of the results of the technical evaluation. To open “Financial Part” of the Bids, Purchaser will request passwords to eligible and qualified Bidders with substantially responsive Technical Parts.

A Bidder, whose “FINANCIAL PART” will be submitted without password protection, or who will disclose their price in the GE-GP system, will be disqualified.

8.   All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid-Securing Declaration.

9. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the Bidding Document.

procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIQUE DU CONGO

Unité - Travail - Progrès

----------------

MINISTERE DE L’ECONOMIE, DU PLAN,

DE LA STATISTIQUE ET DE LA PROSPECTIVE

--------------------------------

PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES EN AFRIQUE DE L’OUEST ET DU CENTRE - SERIE DE PROJETS N°2 (HISWACA - SOP 2)

----------------------------

UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET

---------------------------------

                                                                              

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERÊTS N°079/HISWACA /26 POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL CHARGÉ D’APPUYER LA MISE À JOUR DE LA NOMENCLATURE CONGOLAISE DES ACTIVITÉS (NOCOA) ET DE LA NOMENCLATURE CONGOLAISE DES PRODUITS (RELANCE)

 

1.Le Gouvernement de la République du Congo a reçu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) pour la mise en œuvre des activités du « Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (HISWACA) », et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : «recrutement d’un consultant individuel chargé d’appuyer la mise à jour de la nomenclature congolaise des activités (NOCOA) et de la nomenclature congolaise des produits (NOCOP)».

2. L'objectif général de la mission est d'appuyer l’Institut National de la Statistique (INS) dans la mise à jour de la NOCOA et de la NOCOP conformément aux recommandations internationales de la CITI Rév. 5 et de la CPC 3.0, tout en intégrant les spécificités structurelles de l’économie congolaise. Plus spécifiquement, il s’agira de :

  • Analyser les versions actuellement en vigueur de la NOCOA et de la NOCOP ;
  • Examiner les innovations introduites par la CITI Rév. 5 et la CPC 3.0 ;
  • Identifier les adaptations nécessaires au contexte économique national ;
  • Accompagner les groupes techniques de travail dans la révision des nomenclatures ;
  • Élaborer les projets de nomenclatures actualisées ;
  • Contribuer à la production des tables de correspondance entre anciennes et nouvelles nomenclatures ;
  • Élaborer les notes explicatives nationales ;
  • Contribuer à la préparation du projet de décret instituant l’usage obligatoire des nomenclatures nationales ;
  • Renforcer les capacités techniques des cadres de l’INS ;
  • Appuyer l’organisation et l’animation des ateliers techniques et de validation ;
  • Finaliser les versions actualisées de la NOCOA et de la NOCOP.

3. L’Unité de gestion du projet HISWACA invite les consultants individuels à manifester leur intérêt en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants individuels intéressés doivent fournir les informations sur leur qualifications et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations (curriculum-vitae daté et signé, copies des diplômes et des justificatifs de références en prestations similaires réalisées, etc.)

5.Les consultants peuvent obtenir les termes de références de la mission par courriel à l’adresse : recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com / ugp@hiswaca-congo.org, de 9 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 16 heures (heures locales) du lundi au vendredi.

6.Les manifestations d’intérêts doivent être écrites en langue française et être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous ou envoyées par courriel au plus tard le lundi 05 octobre 2026 (à minuit, heure locale) et porter clairement la mention « Recrutement d’un consultant individuel chargé d’appuyer la mise à jour de la nomenclature congolaise des activités (NOCOA) et de la nomenclature congolaise des produits (NOCOP) ».  

7.L’adresse à laquelle, il est fait référence ci-dessus est : projet HISWACA, Centre d’Affaires des Tours Jumelles de Mpila, 12ième étage, Porte 1204 ;                       Tél : (+242) 06 157 01 01, E-mail : recrutementhiswaca@gmail.com / ugp@hiswaca-congo.org

2.    Le Consultant aura pour mission de réaliser l’étude de faisabilité économique, environnementale et sociale pour la mise en place d’une Zone Economique Spéciale Pilote à Boali en République Centrafricaine. L’objectif de la mission vise à créer les conditions à la viabilisation de la zone économique spéciale de Boali en fournissant une analyse complète permettant de décider ou non de la mise en œuvre d’une ZES pilote.

3. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services. Les dossiers de candidature (20 à 30 pages maximum) comprendront les éléments essentiels suivants :

  1.  Avoir réalisé au moins une (1) étude de faisabilité technique et économique pour la création d’une zone économique spéciale,

 

  1. Disposer du personnel requis pour la mission.

 

  1. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

b) Être capable de mobiliser une équipe de professionnels disposant de qualifications appropriées et d’une solide expérience dans les domaines pertinents du transport urbain et de l’économie.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Selection of Firms)

PEOPLE’S REPUBLIC OF CHINA

World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project)

Loan No.: 9084-CN

Procurement No.: 0733-26094116

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Supervision of the Construction of the Terrestrial Wildlife Disease Surveillance System

Contract No.: HN-FC-58

The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank to finance the World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of the loan to consulting services.

The main scope of the consulting services (hereinafter referred to as the “Services”) includes quality, schedule, cost, and safety control and assurance for all works under the supervision of all 10 monitoring stations; contract management, information management and work coordination; preliminary review of engineering consultations and negotiations; and measurement of completed works for payment of progress payments. The specific scope of services is as follows:

  1. The Chief Supervision Engineer shall be responsible for preparing the supervision plan and submitting it to the Client in a timely manner.
  2. Assist the Client in preparing for the commencement of construction.
  3. Review and approve the contractor’s construction organization plan and construction drawings, and prepare targeted supervision rules.
  4. Coordinate the cooperation among different contractors and trades.
  5. Verify the certificates of conformity, quality assurance certificates, test reports, and other relevant documents for materials and equipment; verify the lists of materials and equipment submitted by the contractor; inspect the specifications, quality, and quantities of materials, components, and equipment used in the works; and conduct sampling and retesting of materials with quality concerns. Unqualified materials shall not be used in the works.
  6. Preside over the review of engineering drawings; within the scope authorized by the Client, sign and confirm engineering design changes and site instructions/variations; regularly preside over weekly supervision meetings and prepare the meeting minutes.
  7. Review and approve the construction schedule, supervise the progress of construction, and supervise the contractor’s compliance with safety requirements. Be responsible for inspecting the quality of the works, conducting witnessed sampling and testing, and recording the test results.
  8. Organize the preliminary inspection of the works and submit rectification recommendations to the Client, and ultimately participate in the completion acceptance of the works.
  9. Supervise the performance of the construction contract.
  10. In accordance with the payment provisions of the construction contract, calculate the quantity of works completed during the month based on the monthly progress plan, and have the Chief Supervision Engineer issue the supporting documentation for the advance payment. Submit monthly supervision reports on a regular basis and maintain supervision logs. Where necessary, prepare special reports within the scope of supervision services, including quality analysis reports, on an ad hoc basis.
  11. Regularly inspect the contractor’s implementation of the specific arrangements and measures under the Project’s Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), record the implementation in the supervision logs, and provide periodic summaries in the monthly supervision reports.
  12. Supervise the construction contractor in carrying out the completion acceptance of the works in accordance with the contract.
  13. Implement dynamic management of the supervision logs throughout the supervision process and establish a supervision work register system for supervision records and documents.
  14. Report special or exceptional issues to the Client in a timely manner.
  15. Be responsible for organizing and completing the procedures for completion acceptance and assist the Client in coordinating with relevant government authorities.

For details, please refer to the Terms of Reference (TOR).

The estimated total input for this consulting service is 66 person-months. The consultants’ services shall commence from the date on which the contract is signed and becomes effective and continue until completion acceptance of the construction project.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this consulting service are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

Hainan Provincial Forestry Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (the “Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide relevant supporting documents in accordance with the following requirements. The Expression of Interest (i.e., the submission) shall include, at a minimum:

  1. A brief introduction to the consulting firm, including its organizational structure, staffing, etc.
  2. A Power of Attorney, identification documents of the legal representative and the authorized representative. If the Consultant is a joint venture, a joint venture agreement (in a format of the Consultant’s own choosing) shall also be provided.
  3. The consulting firm shall have independent legal person status and a valid business license. The Consultant shall provide a copy of its business license or Certificate of Legal Person of a Public Institution.
  4. If the Consultant is a state-owned enterprise or public institution, it shall provide its articles of association and the audited financial audit report and financial statements for 2025, including at least the balance sheet, cash flow statement, and income statement/profit and loss statement.
  5. The Consultant shall possess a Grade B or above qualification for supervision of building construction projects issued by the competent construction administrative authority; or, in accordance with the Notice of the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on Issuing the Reform Plan for the Qualification Management System for Construction Enterprises (Jianshi [2020] No. 94), shall have obtained the corresponding qualification under the new qualification certificate system. The Consultant shall provide a copy of the Grade B or above qualification certificate for supervision of building construction projects issued by the competent construction administrative authority, or relevant supporting documents demonstrating that the corresponding qualification has been obtained under the new qualification certificate system in accordance with the above Notice.
  6. The consulting firm shall possess the Hainan Provincial Construction Enterprise Integrity Record Manual. The Consultant shall provide the page of the Hainan Provincial Construction Enterprise Integrity Record Manual generated by the information platform, duly affixed with the official seal of the entity as required, or equivalent supporting documents.
  7. The consulting firm shall have undertaken and successfully completed at least three (3) supervision projects for building construction works during the past three years (from January 1, 2023 to the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest), with each supervision contract having a contract value of not less than RMB 400,000. Copies of the key pages of the relevant supervision contracts for building construction works shall be provided, including at least the contract cover page, contract date, scope of services, contract amount, contract signature and seal page, and other key information.
  8. Any other information that the Consultant considers necessary to provide (if any).

At this stage, no evaluation of the Consultants will be conducted. The Client will select one (1) consulting firm with the best qualifications and relevant experience from among all consulting firms that have submitted Expressions of Interest, and invite the selected firm to submit its Technical and Financial Proposals and enter into negotiations.

Interested Consultants should take note of the provisions of paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (the “Procurement Regulations”) (November 2020), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflicts of interest.

Consulting firms may associate with other firms when submitting Expressions of Interest to enhance their qualifications, but should clearly indicate whether such association is in the form of a joint venture and/or subcontracting arrangement. If a joint venture is formed, each member of the joint venture shall meet the “Qualification Requirements for Consulting Firms” specified in this Request for Expressions of Interest. If the joint venture is selected, all members of the joint venture and its subcontracted consultants shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire Contract.

The Consultant will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) method specified in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information may be obtained from China CNTIC Tendering Co., Ltd. during working hours, from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on working days.

procnotices.notice_text:
PROJET DE TRANSFORMATION URBAINE ET L’EMPLOI A KINSHASA

(KIN LA BELLE)

PROJET ID : P512210 – IDA- 7996

AVIS GENERAL DE PASSATION DES MARCHES

AGPM N°001/MITP/CI/KIN LA BELLE/2026

 

Date de publication : 10 septembre 2026

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) met en œuvre le Programme de Transformation Urbaine et de Création d'Emplois à Kinshasa, dont la Phase 1 (ci-après « le Projet ») bénéficie d'un crédit de l'Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) d'un montant de 250 millions USD. Ce projet s'inscrit dans le cadre d'une Approche Programmatique Multi-Phase (MPA) d'un montant total de 500 millions USD sur la période 2026–2034.
  2. L'objectif de développement du Programme (ODPr) est de fournir des services de gestion des déchets solides, d'assurer l'accès au front fluvial et à la mobilité urbaine, et de créer des emplois à Kinshasa.
  3. L'objectif de développement du Projet pour la Phase 1 (ODP) est de : (i) fournir des services intégrés de gestion des déchets solides dans des communes sélectionnées ; (ii) développer des capacités et des plans pour l'aménagement du front fluvial ; et (iii) créer des emplois de meilleure qualité et plus inclusifs à Kinshasa.
  4. Ces fonds sont proposés pour régler des fournitures, des travaux et des services devant être acquis dans le cadre de l’exécution du projet KIN LA BELLE qui comprend les 4 composantes ci-après :

Composante 1 :         Services intégrés de gestion des déchets solides dans les communes sélectionnées à Kinshasa

Cette composante vise à améliorer les services de Gestion des Déchets Solides (GDS)-collecte, transport, élimination et valorisation des déchets-dans certaines communes de la ville et à promouvoir des initiatives communautaires de minimisation et de récupération des déchets dans toute la ville. Cette composante vise à rendre le système de gestion de déchets solides de la ville plus efficace et plus attrayant pour la participation du secteur privé en améliorant à la fois son efficacité opérationnelle et sa viabilité financière.

Composante 2 : Connecter les populations à l'espace et aux opportunités

Cette composante aidera le gouvernement à préparer les investissements futurs destinés à accroître l'accès aux débouchés économiques et aux berges de la ville. La phase 1 assure la disponibilité du foncier, la mise en place des conditions techniques et du cadre institutionnel pour un levier structurant de transformation territoriale et économique de Kinshasa, positionnant l’aménagement des berges et le transport fluvial comme un corridor urbain intégré combinant mobilité durable, valorisation foncière et attractivité économique, notamment par une meilleure articulation avec le système global de mobilité urbaine.

 

Composante 3 : Compétitivité pour des emplois inclusifs et croissance économique

Cette composante opérationnalisera une approche intégrée visant à améliorer la prestation des services urbains à Kinshasa, en renforçant les chaînes de valeur structurées dans la gestion des déchets solides (GDS) et la réhabilitation des berges, afin de créer des emplois inclusifs et durables. Elle vise à renforcer le lien entre la fourniture des services urbains et l’emploi inclusif, en mettant en place un vivier structuré d’opportunités d’emplois à court, moyen et long terme à Kinshasa, le long de la chaîne de valeur de la GDS ainsi que dans les secteurs de l’aménagement des berges et du transport fluvial, tout en favorisant l’entrepreneuriat et le développement des compétences pour assurer la durabilité et l’intégration au marché.

Composante 4 : Gestion de projet

Cette composante financera les coûts additionnels de gestion du projet pour l'unité(s) coordination(s) du projet (UGP), ainsi que les honoraires de consultants, les coûts d'audit, la mise en œuvre du Cadre environnemental et social (CES), le suivi et l'évaluation (y compris les données ventilées par sexe). Il financera également une assistance technique ciblée à l’UGP et les deux unités techniques pour soutenir la préparation, la coordination et la mise en œuvre des activités. Le Projet appuiera le renforcement des capacités techniques en matière de gestion des déchets ménagers et en matière de sauvegarde environnementale et social ainsi que le renforcement des dispositifs institutionnels et des systèmes de l’UGP, des prestataires et des agences publiques concernées, via le Centre d’apprentissage ou un prestataire tiers. Cette activité couvrira également les coûts de réinstallation liés à la sécurisation des sites potentiels et emprises

 

  1. Au cours de l’exécution du projet, les marchés seront passés suivant les approches et méthodes de passation des marchés prévue dans le Plan de Passation des Marchés approuvé et conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d'Investissements, édition de Septembre 2025. procnotices.notice_text:
Avis Spécifique d’Appel d’Offres (AA0)

Appel d’Offres pour Fournitures

(Processus à Deux Enveloppes)

Appel d’Offres international No : 2026/03

 N° SN-SAED-486879-GO-RFB

Projet : Programme de résilience du système alimentaire en Afrique de l’Ouest -FSRP.

Acheteur : SAED

Pays : Sénégal

Intitulé du Marché : Fourniture et installation de groupes électropompes, de groupes motopompes et d’équipements solaires pour les stations de pompage de périmètres dans la vallée du fleuve Sénégal dans le cadre du programme de résilience du système alimentaire en Afrique de l’ouest -FSRP.

Crédit No : IDA crédit nº74860

Emis le : 16 septembre 2026

Le Gouvernement du Sénégal a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour                financer le programme de résilience du système alimentaire (FSRP), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre des Marchés de fourniture et installation de groupes électropompes, de groupes moto dans la vallée du fleuve Sénégal dans le cadre du programme de résilience du système alimentaire en Afrique de l’ouest -FSRP. Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, à l’exception des paiements pour lesquels le marché prévoit l’utilisation de crédit documentaire. 

La SAED sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir et d’installer, 10 groupes électropompes, 125 groupes motopompes dont 25 GMP et 100 groupes motopompes GMP sur bacs flottant et leurs accessoires et l’acquisition d’équipements solaires photovoltaïques pour 20 électropompes dans la zone de Dagana, de Podor, de l’île à Morphil, de Matam et de Bakel. Ces prestations sont scindées en quatre (04) lots comme suit :

  • Lot 1 : acquisition et installation d’équipements solaires photovoltaïques pour les     stations de pompage fixes dans les Délégations de Dagana, Matam et Bakel ;
  • Lot 2 : acquisition et installation d’équipements solaires photovoltaïques pour les stations de pompage fixes dans la Délégation de Podor ;
  • Lot 3 : acquisition et installation d’équipements de pompage pour les PIV de Fanaye à Thillé dans la Délégation de Podor ;
  • Lot 4 : acquisition et installation d’équipements de pompage pour les PIV de l’Île à Morphil dans la Délégation de Podor.

Un Soumissionnaire peut présenter une offre pour un ou plusieurs marchés, comme précisé dans le Document d’Appel d’Offres. Un Soumissionnaire désirant offrir un rabais dans le cas où plusieurs marchés leur seraient attribués, seront autorisés à le faire, mais ils devront indiquer ces rabais dans le Formulaire d’Offre.

La passation du Marché sera conduite par la Mise en Concurrence Internationale (AOI) tel que défini dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale (juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Aout 2018, Novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février 2025 et sepetmbre 2025) », et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.

Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. Les pondérations suivantes s'appliqueront aux Critères notés (y compris les facteurs techniques et autres que le prix) : 60% et pour le coût de l'Offre : 40%.

Les Soumissionnaires éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de la SAED ; à la Direction des Aménagements et des Infrastructures Hydroagricoles (DAIH) à  Ngallèle adresse électronique : saeddaih@orange.sn;  et prendre connaissance des      documents d’Appel d’offres durant les  heures de bureau du lundi au jeudi de 8 h 00 mn à 17 h 00 mn et le vendredi de 8 h à 12h 45 mn GMT à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous : Cellule de Passation des Marchés de la SAED, bureau N° 28 premier étage à la Direction Générale de la SAED, RN2, km 10 route de Rosso - Tél. 33 938-22-00 RN2, km 10 Route de Rosso, Saint-Louis – SENEGAL, Téléphone : +221 33 938 22 00, cc : cpm.saed@gmail.com

Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir un dossier d’appel d’offres complet en Français en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous et contre un paiement non remboursable de 100 000 FCFA. La méthode de paiement sera en espèces, chèque certifié au nom de la SAED ou par virement dans le compte numéro SN 048 08001 000210139601 53, LA BANQUE AGRICOLE. Le document d’appel d’offres sera remis aux soumissionnaires par mail ou directement au niveau de la Cellule de Passation des Marchés de la SAED.

Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse suivante à la Cellule de Passation des Marchés de la SAED, bureau N° 28 premier étage à la Direction Générale de la SAED, Ngallèle, RN2, km 10 Route de Rosso, Saint Louis – SENEGAL au plus tard le Jeudi 12 novembre 2026 à 10 heures 00 mn (GMT). La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les enveloppes extérieures des Offres marquées « OFFRE ORIGINALE », et les enveloppes intérieures marquées « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne choisissant d’être présente à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous : Salle de conférence Sidy Mokhtar KEITA à la Direction Générale de la SAED, Ngallèle RN2, km 10 Route de Rosso, Saint Louis – SENEGAL le Jeudi 12 novembre 2026 à 10 heures 00 mn (GMT). Toutes les enveloppes marquées « PARTIE FINANCIERE DEUXIEME ENVELOPPE » devront rester non ouvertes et seront conservées en un lieu sûr par l’Acheteur jusqu’à la deuxième ouverture publique.

Les offres doivent comprendre une Garantie de l’Offre, pour un montant de :

  • 14 000 000 FCFA pour le lot 1 ;
  • 14 000 000 FCFA pour le lot 2 ;
  • 09 000 000 FCFA pour le lot 3 ;
  • 11 000 000 FCFA pour le lot 4.

 L’attention est attirée sur le Règlement de Passation de Marchés exigeant que l’Emprunteur divulgue des informations sur la propriété effective du Soumissionnaire retenu, dans le cadre de la Notification d’Attribution du Marché, en utilisant le Formulaire de Divulgation des Bénéficiaires Effectifs tel qu’il est inclus dans le document d’appel d’offres.

 Le Directeur Général

REPUBLIC OF LIBERIA
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

PROJECT: EXCELLENCE IN LEARNING IN LIBERIA (EXCEL) PROJECT
www.moeliberia.com

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)
(CONSULTING SERVICES)
Individual Consultant Selection (INDV)

 

     ADVERTISED                                                                   September 21, 2026

Assignment Title

Procurement Method

Assignment Duration

 TECHNICAL LEAD FOR MATHEMATICS

Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) Method

Project Duration: 5 years

Contract: 75 days

 

Background

The Government of Liberia has signed financing agreements with the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group to implement the Excellence in Learning in Liberia (EXCEL) Project. The project is co-financed through a Grant from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and a concessional loan/credit from IDA.

 

The project will support the Government in implementing a defined strategy to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system in Liberia. To do this, the project will use a combination of investment project financing and results-based financing.

 

The project’s development objective (PDO) is to improve foundational learning and access in public primary schools and to strengthen the education system.

 

The EXCEL Project is a five-year initiative that aims to drastically reduce learning poverty by improving foundational literacy and numeracy for students in Kindergarten 2 (KG-2) through Grade 6. Current gaps include a severe shortage of high-quality textbooks and a lack of structured, evidence-based pedagogical tools, resulting in low proficiency levels. This assignment will help address these challenges by developing Mathematics Teaching and Learning Materials (TLMs) aligned with the recently updated curriculum standards and the

Global Proficiency Framework (GPF), ensuring all outputs are pedagogically sound, culturally relevant, and foster mastery of core mathematics skills.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for this position can be found in the link below:

  https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ciH8n0d7LDLTXMWl2z5kzIHDo-HGlKkh/edit?usp=drive_link&ouid=107323012285589547376&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Ministry of Education now invites eligible and interested Individual Applicants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the required Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the required Services. The shortlisting (qualification) criteria are listed as per the Terms of Reference. Applicants must have minimum qualifications and experience as per the Terms of Reference.

Applicants will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) as set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated July 2016, as revised in September 2025.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e., 0900 to 1600 hours GMT, Monday to Friday.

The deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest is 2nd October 2026 by 1600 hours (4 pm GMT). Please submit your Expressions of Interest with a letter of interest and your CV to the addresses below, based on your preference, indicating the position title in the subject line of the email/application. All hard-copy applications should be dropped in the designated bid box to be placed at the main entrance security desk at the MoE.

Qualified female candidates are especially encouraged to apply.

  

Please note that ONLY shortlisted Applicants will be contacted.

procnotices.notice_text:
APPEL A CANDIDATURE

RECRUTEMENT DES MEMBRES DE L’UGP (Unité de Gestion du Projet) DU
PROJETS DE RENFORCEMENT DE CAPACITES STATISTIQUES

1. Identification des postes :
Titre des postes :Responsable de Suivi et Évaluation; Responsable en Passation de
Marché; Responsable Administratif et Financier; Comptable.
Direction : INSEED
Superviseur immédiat : Conseil d’Administration de l’INSEED (CA)
Description du projet
L’Institut National de la Statistique des Études Économiques et Démographique (INSEED)
est le chef de file de la production, du traitement et de la diffusion de l’information
statistiques au niveau national. Cette activité est stipulée par l’article 24 de la Loi n°11-
003/AU du 26 mars 2011 portant organisation et règlementation des activités statistiques
aux Comores. L’INSEED a bénéficié des Fonds fiduciaire pour le renforcement des
capacités statistiques (TFSCB) de la Banque Mondiale en 2014-2015 et du projet « statistique
de Comores » financé par la Banque Mondiale pendant la période de 2017 à
2020. Ces projets ont apporté une multitude de résultats concrets répondant aux besoins
de Comores en matière de statistiques à l’instar de l’institutionnalisation de l’INSEED
(crée en 2014), de la quatrième édition du Recensement Général de la
Population et de l’Habitat (RGPH4), de l’Enquête Harmonisée des Conditions de Vies
de Ménages (EHCVM20), des nouveaux statisticiens agricoles et des cadres de l’INSEED
renforcés en formations ponctuelle. Afin de maintenir les acquis de ces projets
et d’améliorer davantage la capacité en statistique en Union de Comores, l’INSEED,
avec l’appui de la Banque Mondiale entame le projet d’investissement de soutien aux
capacités statistiques de la communauté de développement de l’Afrique australe.
Ainsi, l’INSEED souhaite recruter les membres de l’Unité de Gestion du Projet aux
postes suivantes : Responsable de Suivi et Évaluation; Responsable en Passation de
Marché; Responsable Administratif et Financier et Comptable
Les candidats intéressés sont priés d’écrire à l’adresse mail suivante pour les
TDR et l’envoie des dossiers : recrutement.statcap@gmail.com

Government of Sudurpashchim Province

Works

(Two-envelope Bidding Process Without Prequalification)

Employer: Provincial Project Management Unit (PPMU), Dhangadhi, Kailali, Nepal

Project: Provincial and Local Roads Improvement Program (PLRIP)

Contract title: Construction and upgradation works of Shreebhawar-Dogad-Garje Road of Baitadi District

Country: Nepal

Loan No. /Credit No. / Grant No.: P171836 (Loan)

RFB No: PLRIP/SUPA/BTD/W/ICB/NC/01/082-83

Issued on: September 21, 2026

 

1. The Government of Nepal [GoN] has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Provincial and Local Roads Improvement Program (PLRIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Construction and upgradation works of Shreebhawar-Dogad-Garje Road of Baitadi District.

2. The Provincial Project Management Unit (PPMU), Dhangadhi, Kailali invites sealed bids from eligible Bidders for the procurement of Construction and upgradation works of Shreebhawar-Dogad-GarjeRoad of Baitadi District. The construction period is Two years six months (2.5 years). The works consists of two phases: (a) Phase: 1 Construction and upgradation works - The Construction and upgradation works of Shreebhawar-Dogad-Garje Road of Baitadi District consisting of the Site Clearance, Earthworks. flexible pavement construction, rigid pavement construction, Road safety and traffic management work, retaining structures, bridge, culverts, drain and bio-engineering works, etc., and (b) Phase 2: Performance Based Maintenance Works for 5 years (Maintenance works consisting of all activities to be carried out to achieve and keep the road assets as defined in the Technical Specifications) after completion of Construction and Upgradation works, under International Competitive Bidding – Single Stage Two Envelope Bidding procedures. Both phases will be awarded under this procurement but phase 1 (upgrading works) will be fully funded by the World Bank whilst the phase 2 (maintenance works) will be funded by the government of Nepal. 

3. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulation for IPF Borrowers, 7th edition dated September 2025” (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 50 %. and for Bid cost: 50  %.

5. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information and inspect the bidding documents during the office hours (i.e., 9:00 to 17:00 hours) at the address given below or at the Website: https://plripppmu.sudurpashchim.gov.np/

6. A single-stage, two envelope RFB process will be used, and the Proposal will consist of (i) the Technical Part, without any reference to prices; and (ii) the Financial Part, as detailed in the RFB Document. The Bidding document in English may be purchased by interested eligible Bidders upon the submission of a written application at the address below and upon payment of a nonrefundable fee NRs 20,000.00 (In Words: Twenty Thousand Only) or US$ 150. Alternatively, bidding documents may also be downloaded from the website: https://plripppmu.sudurpashchim.gov.np, but would be required to pay the indicted amount in the event of submission of bid. The method of payment will be direct deposit to the following account:

Information to deposit the cost of bidding document in Bank:

Name of the Bank: Rastriya Banijya Bank Ltd, Dhangadhi

Name of Office: Provincial and Local Roads Improvement Program (PLRIP), Provincial Project Management Unit (PPMU), Sudurpashchim Province, Dhangadhi, Kailali

Office Code no.: 3370177027                  

Office Account no.: 1000100200010000

Rajaswa (revenue) Shirshak no.: 14229

7. Bids, both Technical and Financial must be submitted in hard copy, at the address below by hand/courier on or before 12:00 hours (Nepal Standard Time) on November 13, 2026. The outer Bid envelopes marked “ORIGINAL BID”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on Provincial Project Management Unit (PPMU), Dhangadhi, Kailali., 13:00 hours on November 13, 2026. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Employer until the second public Bid opening. Electronic bidding will not be permitted.

8. Late Bids will be rejected. The “TECHNICAL PART” of the bid will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below immediately after bid submission deadline on November 13, 2026 at 13:00 hrs. “FINANCIAL PART” of the bid shall remain unopened until the second public Bid opening, notified after completion of evaluation of Technical Part of the bid.

9. All Bids must be accompanied by a: (i) “Bid Security” of US$ 336,000.00 or NPR 51,412,000.00, (ii) Local Labour Method Statement and iii) Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) and/or Sexual Harassment (SH) Declaration.  Bids must be valid until March 12, 2027.  Bids must be accompanied by a Original copy of the bid security which shall be valid until April 11, 2027.

10. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

SOCIAL OFFICER (Local) - (FULL-TIME)

Preparation for Fiji Energy Transformation Project

Project Preparation Unit (PPU) | Energy Fiji Limited (EFL)
World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF)

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project

Implementing Agency

Assignment Title

Social Officer (Local) - (Full-Time)

Organisational Unit

Project Preparation Unit (PPU)

Primary Framework

World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF)

Duty Station / Coverage

PPU office, with regular field visits across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni

Reporting Line

Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist; PPU Project Manager on overall project matters

Expected Commencement

As soon as possible

Table of Contents

Table of Contents. 1

3.5 Gender and Vulnerability. 4

3.6 Labor and Working Conditions - Social Dimensions. 4

3.9 Reporting and Coordination. 5

4. Methodology and Approach. 5

5. Key Deliverables and Indicative Timing. 6

6. Assignment Duration and Work Programme. 6

7.2 Professional Experience. 6

7.3 Skills and Competencies. 7

8. Reporting and Working Arrangements. 7

9. Application Requirements. 7

 

 

 

1. Introduction and Background

The Fiji Energy Transformation Project is proposed as a USD 230 million World Bank-supported initiative aimed at accelerating renewable energy, modernizing the power grid, and reforming the energy sector to attract private investment. Key interventions include large-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) parks of 50 MW or more each, grid evacuation infrastructure, transmission line upgrades, and modernization of existing power stations across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. The project’s environmental and social risks have been classified as Substantial under the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

A significant portion of land in the project area is held under customary iTaukei tenure and managed through the iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB). Many affected communities are iTaukei Fijians who qualify as Indigenous Peoples under ESS7. The project may also involve economic and physical displacement linked to land acquisition for solar parks, transmission lines, and associated infrastructure, triggering ESS5 on Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement.

The Social Officer will be embedded within the PPU and will work under the day-to-day supervision of the Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist, who has overall leadership of the project’s E&S function. The Social Officer will work in close coordination with the Environment Officer. Together, these positions constitute the project’s E&S team and are jointly responsible for delivering the suite of ESF instruments required for project appraisal and for supporting implementation thereafter.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the timely preparation of all social-related ESF instruments required for appraisal, ensure ongoing and meaningful stakeholder engagement throughout project preparation and implementation, and serve as the PPU’s primary liaison with government line ministries and agencies responsible for land, indigenous affairs, and social protection.

3. Scope of Work

3.1 Stakeholder Engagement and Community Liaison

a. Lead the preparation, implementation, and updating of the project’s Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), in close coordination with the E&S Specialist, who will review and finalize the instrument. The SEP must include:

  • A project-wide grievance redress mechanism (GRM), including a reporting structure for complaint escalation and resolution within specified timeframes.
  • A dedicated pathway for Sexual Exploitation and Abuse / Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) complaints, including resolution or escalation timeframes.
  • Differentiated engagement approaches for iTaukei communities, women, and other vulnerable groups.
  • A disclosure schedule compliant with ESF requirements.

b. Serve as the PPU’s primary point of contact for community-level consultations across project sites on Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. Coordinate field consultation logistics with the Environment Officer so that environmental and social consultations are sequenced and, where possible, combined to minimize the burden on communities.

c. Maintain a consultation log recording meetings, attendees disaggregated by gender and community role, issues raised, and follow-up actions. Share the log with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer on a fortnightly basis.

d. Ensure that Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes are properly documented for all iTaukei communities in the project’s area of influence, in accordance with ESS7 and applicable Fijian law.

3.2 Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF)

a. Lead the preparation of the Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF) in accordance with ESS7. The IPPF must:

  • Liaise with the EFL Lands Team to identify all iTaukei communities and landowning units (mataqali) in the project’s area of influence.
  • Set out a methodology for social assessment and FPIC at the site-specific level.
  • Define entitlements and culturally appropriate benefit-sharing mechanisms.
  • Establish culturally sensitive grievance and feedback channels.
  • Address gender dynamics and vulnerabilities within iTaukei communities.

b. Coordinate with the E&S Specialist to ensure consistency between the IPPF, the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and the SEP, so that the instruments present a coherent and non-contradictory framework for community engagement and entitlements.

c. Where site-specific Indigenous Peoples Plans (IPPs) are required, support their preparation in parallel with, or as a follow-on to, the IPPF.

3.3 Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF)

a. Support the E&S Specialist in preparing the RPF in accordance with ESS5. The Social Officer will be responsible for:

  • Conducting or supervising social baseline surveys required to inform the RPF.
  • Documenting existing land use, livelihoods, and community assets in project-affected areas.
  • Drafting the entitlement matrix in coordination with the E&S Specialist.
  • Ensuring that the RPF reflects the specificities of iTaukei land tenure and customary rights.

b. Coordinate with the Environment Officer to ensure that environmental footprint assessments underpinning the RPF, including site boundaries, buffer zones, and access routes, are accurate and consistently applied across instruments.

3.4 Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence

a. Support the E&S Specialist in preparing the Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report. The Social Officer will:

  • Coordinate with the EFL Lands Team and liaise with the TLTB and relevant landowning units (mataqali) to understand existing or proposed negotiated land agreements for solar park and transmission line sites.
  • Verify the voluntariness of negotiations and document indicators of undue pressure or inadequate community representation.
  • Identify gaps between existing agreements and ESF requirements and propose remediation measures.

3.5 Gender and Vulnerability

a. Integrate gender analysis into all social instruments, ensuring that the project identifies and responds to differential impacts on women, girls, and other vulnerable or marginalized groups.

b. Support the preparation of a Gender Action Plan or equivalent measures, in coordination with the E&S Specialist.

c. Identify and document vulnerable households in the project area, including elderly people, persons with disabilities, female-headed households, and households with insecure tenure, and ensure they are reflected in the RPF entitlement matrix and the IPPF.

3.6 Labor and Working Conditions - Social Dimensions

a. Contribute to the Labor Management Procedures (LMP) by preparing the social dimensions, including community hiring provisions, management of labor influx risks, SEA/SH and communicable disease risks in host communities, supply chain social due diligence requirements, and conflict resolution between workers and community members. The E&S Specialist retains overall responsibility for the LMP.

b. Coordinate with the Environment Officer on environmental health dimensions of labor influx, including waste, water, and camp management, to ensure that the LMP presents unified and internally consistent measures.

3.7 Coordination with Government Line Ministries and Agencies

The Social Officer will serve as the PPU’s primary liaison with the following entities on social matters:

  • Ministry of Lands and Mineral Resources: land acquisition procedures, state land matters, and coordination of required land surveys or valuations.
  • iTaukei Affairs Board / Ministry of iTaukei Affairs: customary governance, community protocols, and support for FPIC processes.
  • iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB): management of iTaukei land, negotiated agreements, lease arrangements, and consent from landowning units.
  • Department of Social Welfare / Ministry of Women, Children and Poverty Alleviation: identification of vulnerable households and gender considerations.
  • Any other relevant agency identified during preparation as having a mandate over affected communities or social protection matters.

The Social Officer will establish and maintain regular contact with focal points in each agency, keep records of correspondence and meetings, and report on ministry engagement to the E&S Specialist as part of the fortnightly joint E&S team update.

3.8 Capacity Building

a. Together with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer, contribute to the preparation of the TOR for EFL’s institutional Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS), specifically the social management components.

b. Provide on-the-job guidance to EFL staff engaged in community liaison activities during project preparation.

3.9 Reporting and Coordination

a. Prepare monthly progress reports on social preparation activities and submit them to the E&S Specialist for integration into the consolidated E&S team report to the PPU Project Manager.

b. Maintain a live Social Risk Register tracking identified social risks and mitigation measures, updated fortnightly and shared with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer.

c. Participate in the mandatory weekly joint E&S team meeting and the fortnightly joint risk register review.

d. Coordinate all field visits jointly with the Environment Officer and E&S Specialist. Where a visit has environmental and social dimensions, the Social Officer and Environment Officer will attend together wherever possible to minimize multiple visits and support integrated data collection.

e. Before submitting an instrument draft to the E&S Specialist, circulate it to the Environment Officer for a peer consistency check covering site boundaries, affected population figures, and mitigation commitments.

f. Support the E&S Specialist during World Bank supervision missions and technical reviews, including preparation of briefing materials and attendance at relevant meetings.

4. Methodology and Approach

The Social Officer will apply an integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approach throughout the assignment. The approach will include:

  • Desktop review of available project documents, land information, consultation records, and relevant social baseline information.
  • Field-based social assessment and community consultation across relevant project locations.
  • Culturally appropriate engagement with iTaukei communities and landowning units, including documentation of FPIC where required.
  • Coordination with the E&S Specialist, Environment Officer, EFL Lands Team, government agencies, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Preparation, review, updating, and consistency checking of social instruments and associated records.
  • Routine monitoring through consultation logs, the Social Risk Register, progress reports, and agreed coordination meetings.

5. Key Deliverables and Indicative Timing

All deliverables are subject to World Bank review and clearance. The primary target is project appraisal. Specific submission dates will be agreed with the E&S Specialist and PPU Project Manager upon commencement.

6. Assignment Duration and Work Programme

The position is expected to commence as soon as possible and will cover the full project preparation period through appraisal, with the possibility of extension into implementation. Upon commencement, the Social Officer will agree detailed submission dates, priorities, and an activity schedule with the E&S Specialist and PPU Project Manager. Regular field travel will be required.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

7.1 Education

  • A university degree in social sciences, anthropology, development studies, law, or a related field. A postgraduate degree is an advantage.

7.2 Professional Experience

  • A minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in social safeguards or social risk management on infrastructure or energy projects.
  • Demonstrated experience with World Bank ESF instruments, including ESS1, ESS2, ESS5, ESS7 and ESS10, or equivalent IFC Performance Standards.
  • Demonstrated experience working with Indigenous Peoples and customary land tenure systems in the Pacific or comparable contexts.
  • Experience liaising with government land administration agencies. Familiarity with Fiji’s iTaukei land tenure system and the role of the TLTB is a strong advantage.

7.3 Skills and Competencies

  • Strong facilitation and consultation skills, including experience conducting consultations with rural and indigenous communities.
  • Strong coordination, record-keeping, analytical, and report-writing skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary E&S and project preparation team.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of iTaukei Fijian or Fiji Hindi is an advantage.

8. Reporting and Working Arrangements

The Social Officer is a full-time position based at the PPU office, with regular field visits to project sites across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. The Social Officer reports to the E&S Specialist on a day-to-day basis and to the PPU Project Manager on overall project matters. The Social Officer will participate in the weekly joint E&S team meeting and the broader PPU team meeting.

9. Application Requirements

Interested candidates should submit a curriculum vitae and a cover letter describing their relevant experience in relation to the scope of work set out in this TOR. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Tender documents may be viewed and downloaded from www.efl.com.fj(opens in new window) or https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window).

Submissions by email or facsimile will not be accepted and will be deemed null and void. Hard copy submissions to the tender box at EFL Head Office, Suva, will not be accepted.

FEDERATED STATES OF MICRONESIA

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

Country

Federated States of Micronesia

Project

Project for Strengthening Public Financial Management II (P181237)

Project Implementing Agency / Client

Department of Finance and Administration (DOFA)

Assignment Title

FMIS Advisor

Selection Method

Individual Consultant Selection

Contract Type

Time Based 

Reference No.

FM-DOFA-572432-CS-INDV

Credit/Grant No.

IDA-E4120

Deadline for Submission

October 9, 2026

The Government of The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Public Financial Management II Project (P181237) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve providing full-time technical advisory, implementation oversight and quality assurance support for Component 2 – Expanded Core Financial Management Information Systems (FMIS) of the PFM II Project.

The FMIS Advisor will support the Government in the continued rollout, expansion, effective use and institutionalization of the FMIS across National Government Departments and Agencies and, where applicable, State Governments. The assignment will focus on ensuring that FMIS implementation is aligned with Government's public financial management requirements, business processes, controls and reporting needs, while strengthening Government capacity and reducing reliance on external support.

The key responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:

  • Provide technical advice and coordination support for the FMIS rollout, expansion and related PFM reforms;
  • Support FMIS readiness, implementation, testing, data migration, business process review and quality assurance;
  • Review and monitor FMIS vendor deliverables, system documentation, implementation progress, issues and risks;
  •  Support training, knowledge transfer, capacity building and the development of sustainable Government FMIS support arrangements; and
  • Provide technical inputs to FMIS-related procurement, contracts, technical specifications, implementation teams and governance structures.

The assignment will be based in Palikir, Pohnpei, Federated States of Micronesia, with travel to the four State Governments as required. The assignment is expected to be full-time for twenty-four (24) months, with an anticipated start date as soon as possible, subject to completion of the selection and contracting process.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the Department of Finance and Administration website: https://dofa.gov.fm, as part of this REOI, or can be obtained at the address given below.

The Department of Finance and Administration now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultants should submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV) describing their qualifications, professional experience, experience in similar assignments and relevant experience in similar institutional or country contexts together with a cover letter outlining their interest in the assignment and suitability for the position.

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Mandatory Requirements:

The Consultant shall possess:

  1. A minimum Master's degree in public finance, financial management, accounting, information systems, business administration, economics, public administration, or related field from a recognized university;
  2. At least seven (7) years of professional experience in public financial management, including demonstrated experience in PFM reform, financial management systems or related public sector reform activities at a senior professional level; and
  3. Functional hands-on experience with FreeBalance for at least one government FMIS project, including experience in implementation, rollout, upgrade, migration, testing, quality assurance and/or operational support; and
  4. A proven track record in managing or supporting large-scale ERP/IFMIS/FMIS implementation activities, including system build or configuration, testing, rollout and quality assurance, preferably in developing countries.

Desirable :

  1. Demonstrated experience in business process review and re-engineering, data migration, testing, user acceptance testing and/or operational acceptance testing for an FMIS or ERP;
  2. Experience in vendor management and technical quality assurance, including reviewing FMIS implementation deliverables, system documentation, technical specifications and implementation plans;
  3. Experience in developing and implementing FMIS sustainability, knowledge-transfer and transition arrangements to strengthen government ownership and reduce reliance on external consultants; and
  4. Experience working with government institutions in Asia - Pacific island countries and/or similarly remote Small Island Developing States (SIDS), including experience coordinating multidisciplinary and multicultural stakeholders.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 17:00 hours, Pohnpei Time.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by e-mail only preferably by 5pm Pohnpei Time, October 9, 2026. Expressions of Interest must be submitted by email only to the following addresses:

Attn: Project Manager PFM II

Department of Finance and Administration

P.O Box PS-158

Palikir, Pohnpei, Federated States of Micronesia

Email: osbert.atusaasiire@dofa.gov.fm

And cc: arrio.abello@dofa.gov.fm

 

ANNEX 1: TERMS OF REFERENCE

FEDERATED STATES OF MICRONESIA

Project for Strengthening Public Financial Management II (P181237)

Terms of Reference – Financial Management Information Systems Advisor

Title:

Financial Management Information Systems Advisor

Location:

Palikir, National Government of the Federated States of Micronesia - Department of Finance and Administration (DoFA)

Duration:

Initial contract duration of 2 years (full time) with the potential to extend based on available finance and satisfactory performance

Tentative Start Date:

As soon as possible

A. BACKGROUND

The Government of the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), with support from the World Bank, are working to improve fiscal management practices and increase fiscal transparency at the National Government level through the Strengthening Public Financial Management II Project (P181237).  The project builds upon key public financial management (PFM) achieved under the previous PFM I project and intends to institutionalize those achievements by:

  • Expanding the core financial management information system (FMIS) to line departments and agencies
  • Improve systems and process in budget formulation and execution, procurement, treasury functions, internal controls, and reporting
  • Strengthening technical capacities of the Department of Finance & Administration (DoFA)
  • Review existing PFM legislation to identify changes to support transition to a digital PFM environment

The project components are: (i) improved fiscal management practices and controls, (ii) expanded core FMIS, (iii) enhanced human resource capacity, communications and change management, and (iv) project management.

B. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THE ROLE

Purpose of the assignment

The Consultant primarily support activities under Component 2- Expanded Core Financial Management Information Systems. This component aims at supporting increasing efficiency and automation of public finance processes through the expanded use of the Financial Management Information System (FMIS) implemented under PFM I to additional Government Departments, Agencies and State Governments (where applicable).

Objective of the assignment

The objective of this role is to provide technical support and advisory services to the implementation of public financial management reforms with specific focus on the use of FMIS. With the support of the National Treasury team, the Consultant will drive the further adoption and expansion Financial Management Information System (FMIS) capabilities across core Treasury processes and support the decentralization of the system.

C. SCOPE OF SERVICES

  1. The scope of responsibility will cover:
    • Roll-out and deepen the use of FMIS, including roll out of modules such as fixed assets, payroll, budget and e-procurement.
    • Support for the PFM reforms in general, development and implementation of PFM policies and procedures, capacity building for staff, quality control for policy and general pronouncements and presentations/reports, monitoring and evaluation and other related matters
  2. The FMIS Advisor’s key activities relating above responsibilities will include the following: 
    • Provide technical assistance to the Secretary Department of Finance and Administration (DoFA)and the Assistant Secretary Treasury Comptroller to coordinate and guide the implementation of public financial management reforms and in resolving issues pertaining to the FMIS roll-out. This coordination will involve various streams of activities necessary to make the roll out of the FMIS successful including but not limited to, Training, Acceptance Testing, data migration, Change Management, User authorizations/ security in FMIS and business process reengineering.
    • Work with the PFMII ICT Advisor to ensure that the local area network and the wide area network supports the efficient and effective use of the FMIS system.
    • In line with the FMIS rollout strategy, assess readiness for expansion of the FMIS system to Departments and Agencies in terms of institutional structures, staff availability, capacity and skills, financial management processes and systems (manual or otherwise) and controls, site infrastructure and power, implementation risks and make very specific recommendations to address gaps.
    • Business Process Re-engineering: provide technical support to review PFM processes and Government-on-Line business requirements to determine any necessary validation or re-engineering.
    • Implementation:   prepare and update the Project Plan, the training content/materials and plan, and the change management plan to ensure that the weaknesses and recommendations in the original or modified form, are carried out and implemented.
    • Quality Assurance and OAT (Operational Acceptance Testing): Carry out quality review and assurance to the FMIS Implementation phases including but not limited to the following:
      • Data collection, validation and conversion
      • Equipment and solution deployment
      • Site and infrastructure preparation
      • Testing scripts and User Acceptance testing
      • Training (including training materials) and change management
      • Handling of implementation issues
      • Participation in implementation teams/working groups/ steering committee meetings.
  3. Coordinate with Budget Department to ensure an FMIS system supports the requirements of budgeting and payroll.
  4. Provide the necessary support and guidance to the Assistant Secretary Treasury in order to ensure that all system documentation expected from the FMIS Supplier is delivered or developed including establishing criteria to be applied to review and evaluate all such documents.
  5. Monitoring: the Advisor will draw-up a monitoring framework and periodically monitor and assess the state of implementation particularly focusing on qualitative improvements; the Advisor will review improvements in institutional capacity and training, overall adaptation and use of the FMIS, improvements in financial management processes and systems controls and reporting, and improvements in all aspects of the PFM necessary to meet the overall objectives. Resulting from this process, the Advisor will:
    • Determine areas that may lag or new areas that require attention and make recommendations for improvements
    • Raise issues (technical or otherwise) that may impede progress
  6. The Advisor will develop a plan by which the Government-on-Line will gradually take over full support of its PFM Systems to reduce the Government-on-LIne dependency on external consultants, increase ownership and allow National and State Treasury Staff to manage with the limited resources. Suitable officers / employees should be identified and trained to make this happen. This plan shall be discussed with the Secretary DoFA and approved for implementation. In drawing up this plan, the Advisor will among others:
    • Assess the state of readiness of National and State Government to take over in terms of staff capacity.
    • Determine actions and time required to cover the gaps for example in terms of training, staff recruitment, etc.
    • Determine work plans and milestones to implement these actions. The work plan shall include monitoring meetings with the Steering Committee. The Advisor will help to monitor the implementation of the agreed plan.
  7. Advise on suitable Governance structures required for the management of all the implementation phases of the FMIS.
  8. Throughout the duration of the Project, assisting the Assistant Secretary Treasury to identify risks to the FMIS rollout activities and formulate strategies to mitigate such risks.
  9. Where necessary, review for quality and alignment, technical specifications or Terms of reference to be used in the procurement of PFM related resources.
  10. Provide technical inputs to the IFMIS implementation contracts, procurements and financial management teams

Key Deliverables

No.

Key Deliverable

Timing/Frequency

1

FMIS Technical Advisory and Rollout Support: Provide technical advice and planning support for FMIS rollout to Departments, Agencies, and National and State Governments, including rollout plans, readiness assessments, technical support submissions and recommendations. Support progress towards IR-4 – FMIS rolled out to sectoral Departments.

Throughout the assignment; plans and technical submissions updated or provided as required.

2

FMIS Enhancement and Quality Assurance Support: Provide technical support and quality assurance for FMIS enhancements, interfaces and additional modules, including fixed assets, payroll, budget and e-procurement, as applicable. Support business process review, data migration, testing and review of vendor deliverables. The Advisor shall provide technical advice, oversight and quality assurance and shall not be responsible for system development, configuration or delivery, which remains the responsibility of the FMIS vendor.

Throughout the assignment, in accordance with the approved implementation plan.

3

FMIS Monitoring and Reporting: Prepare technical progress reports covering FMIS rollout, implementation, issues, risks and recommendations, including technical inputs supporting IR-4 and PDO-2 – Number of key fiscal documents made publicly available by DoFA within the timeline specified in PEFA Indicator PI-9.1.

Monthly; annually; and final report before completion of the assignment.

4

Capacity Building, Risk Management and Sustainability: Support FMIS training and knowledge transfer; prepare and update the FMIS Risk Management Plan; and prepare and update an FMIS Sustainability and Transition Plan.

Throughout the assignment; Risk Plan within 3 months and updated periodically; Sustainability Plan within 6 months, updated annually and finalized before completion.

D. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE

The prospective consultant shall be a highly experienced practitioner with a proven record in FMIS Implementation in the public sector internationally. The position will require cross-cultural interpersonal skills to coordinate and negotiate resources across multiple stakeholders in order to achieve positive project outcomes. 

Mandatory 

  1. Minimum Master's degree in public finance, financial management, accounting, information systems, business administration, economics, public administration or related field from a recognized university.
  2. Functional hands-on experience with FreeBalance for at least one government FMIS project.
  3. At least 7 years’ experience in the area of public financial management, including experience with PFM reform processes at a senior level either with Government or large international organizations.
  4. Experience in post conflict environments is desirable.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience:

  1. Strong analytical, oral and written communication skills, report writing, and the ability to write for and present to a variety of stakeholder hierarchies;
  2. A proven track record of successful management of application build, testing, implementation and quality assurance activities of large-scale ERP/IFMIS systems in developing countries is required.
  3. Fluency in English.
  4. Experience working in the Pacific.

F. DURATION, LOCATION and CONDITIONS of ASSIGNMENT

  • The Consultant will report of the Assistant Secretary for Treasury.
  • This is a full-time position for an initial period of Twenty Four (24) Months, based in Palikir, Pohnpei, and may be extended based on satisfactory performance and availability of funding.
  • Domestic travel may be required from time to time, including overnight travel away from the home office.
  • The Department of Finance and Administration will provide office space, general office supplies, and office equipment.

ANNEX B: CONSULTANT’S REPORTING OBLIGATIONS

The Advisor shall submit the following reports during the 24-month assignment:

  1. Monthly Progress Reports: The FMIS Advisor shall prepare and submit a concise monthly progress report covering activities undertaken during the reporting period, progress against the approved FMIS implementation and rollout plan, progress toward relevant PFM II Results Framework indicators, particularly PDO-2 and IR-4, key achievements, emerging issues, risks, corrective actions and matters requiring clarification or decision by the Client.
  2. Annual Progress Reports: The FMIS Advisor shall prepare and submit an annual progress report summarizing progress during each 12-month period of the assignment. The report shall highlight achievements against the approved FMIS implementation and rollout plan, progress toward relevant PFM II Results Framework targets, particularly PDO-2 – Number of key fiscal documents made publicly available by DoFA within the timeline specified in PEFA Indicator PI-9.1 and IR-4 – FMIS rolled out to sectoral Departments, emerging issues and risks, actions taken to address implementation constraints, and recommendations to support successful FMIS implementation and sustainability.
  3. Final Report: Before the end of the 24-month assignment, the FMIS Advisor shall submit a final report documenting all major activities undertaken, achievements against the FMIS implementation and rollout plan, progress against relevant PFM II Results Framework indicators, particularly PDO-2 and IR-4, outstanding issues and risks, lessons learned, knowledge transfer and capacity-building outcomes, sustainability arrangements, and recommendations for the continued implementation and institutionalization of the FMIS.

  1. Formation académique :

    • Une formation spécialisée en suivi-évaluation de projets et programmes de développement constitue un atout majeur.
  2. Expérience professionnelle :
  • Justifier d’une expérience professionnelle générale d’au moins sept (07) ans dans la planification, le suivi-évaluation ou la gestion de projets et programmes de développement ;
  • Justifier d’au moins cinq (05) ans d’expérience spécifique comme spécialiste en suivi évaluation dans des projets financés par des bailleurs (Banque mondiale, BAD, UE, etc.) et d’une bonne connaissance de leurs exigences en matière de reporting ;
  • Une expérience de la conduite d’enquêtes de terrain et d’évaluations d’impact constitue un atout.
